items.title: Beyond 2020: Future of Web Development, Drupal, and our Careers
items.full_description:
Josh Koenig

Sponsored Talk at DrupalCon Europe 2020.

A keynote address exploring the future of web development, Drupal, and careers in the field beyond 2020.

items.title: A magazine approach for storytelling
items.full_description:
Ina Widmer

This session uses schweizerfleisch.ch as a case study to demonstrate how Drupal supports magazine-based storytelling approaches and the flexibility that taxonomy systems provide.

The session examines why Drupal suits this content strategy from multiple angles. From a business and end-user perspective, it highlights how 'a magazine with basic knowledge of Swiss meat' serves both consumers and gastro-professionals. The editor and technical teams benefit from a content model that improves 'content mediation and user guidance.'

Attendees will learn advantages of magazine-style approaches, how taxonomies enable segmentation and filtering, and their role in SEO improvements.

The platform's ability to display content across multiple locations proved essential. The team employed a progressive decoupled approach, with the most critical feature being filterable taxonomy that generates content page URLs dynamically. This creates numerous specific detail pages while grouping content by sections for easy discovery of related historical topics.

items.title: Automated advanced visual regression testing
items.full_description:
Shwetaneel Sharma

In today's digital transformation environment, organizations face pressure to deliver shorter release cycles while maintaining quality. Frontend testing across multiple browsers, operating systems, and devices is time-consuming and error-prone when done manually. Automating visual regression tests has become essential for ensuring visually perfect user experiences alongside functional quality.

The presentation covers automated visual testing fundamentals, including algorithm basics, test creation, execution, and result interpretation. Key challenges discussed include anti-aliasing effects, dynamic content handling, and false positives.

The speaker demonstrates available tools addressing these challenges and outlines strategic approaches for test suite design, such as optimizing screenshot capture methods and execution across device matrices.

Additional topics include CI/CD pipeline integration challenges, market tool comparisons, and getting started guidance for both non-technical and experienced developers.

Attendees will understand what automated visual regression testing is, how it functions, its advantages and challenges, best practices, available tools, implementation timing, and CI cycle integration strategies.

items.title: Building diversity job boards with Drupal
items.full_description:
merlinzant
Jobiqo

The presentation focuses on creating inclusive job board solutions using Drupal technology. The speaker shares case studies of specialized employment platforms built for underrepresented communities, including boards for people with disabilities (e.g. myability.jobs), LGBTI (e.g. lgbti-jobs.ch), people above 50 (50plus-jobs.ch) and other diversity based job boards.

Jobiqo operates as a leading job board software provider built on Drupal. The company has helped more than 80 customers in more than 18 countries globally to launch over 200 job boards. Their stated vision is to enhance online job searching experiences through flexible and personalized matching capabilities.

items.title: Custom Elements: Alternate Render API for decoupled Drupal
items.full_description:
Wolfgang Ziegler

The Custom Elements module allows developers to decouple frontend architecture while preserving Drupal's built-in capabilities. This approach maintains full page caching, layout builder functionality, and editorial control over URL paths.

The module transforms Drupal into an API backend for component-based, decoupled frontends by rendering content into custom elements. Key features include:

- Rendering entities as custom elements
- Providing custom blocks, routes and API endpoints
- Caching and cache metadata handling
- Frontend connection methods
- Preview and custom layout enablement

Related Resources:
https://www.drupal.org/project/custom_elements
https://www.drupal.org/project/lupus_ce_renderer

items.title: Gitlab deep dive for Drupal developers
items.full_description:
VladimirAus

GitLab functions as 'a complete DevOps platform' with capabilities that many users have not fully explored. This discovery session aims to enhance development and operations workflows for web applications.

The session covers application packaging for releases, security testing practices, application monitoring, and reports and notifications.

Attendees will discover how to strengthen continuous integration automation with security scanning capabilities. The session demonstrates improving continuous deployment processes across different hosting environments like Acquia and Platform.sh while maintaining environment flexibility.

Participants will explore monitoring tools that consolidate application and environmental logs into GitLab dashboards. The session emphasizes creating visibility into application status through client reports and developer notifications.

While designed primarily for developers and operations professionals, the content interests technical project managers seeking process improvements through GitLab's capabilities.

items.title: Is your new UX project getting you worried?
items.full_description:
Archita Arora

The session addresses concerns about selecting a UX design agency partner for digital projects. The presenter notes that many struggle with a core worry: 'would they be able to understand our brand?'

Outsourcing brand identity elements can create significant stress and mental fatigue. The session aims to discuss why a design partner matters, how to identify the right one, and how to ensure successful outcomes.

Participants will explore a three-step process—Identify, Cultivate, Activate—to select an appropriate UX design agency.

Key Takeaways:
- Identifying indicators of strong UX expertise
- Effectively budgeting for UX projects
- Creating vendor assessment checklists
- Requesting work proposals effectively
- Evaluating vendor community involvement in Drupal
- Trusting your instincts in decision-making

Target Audience: Project managers, executives, UX designers, sales practitioners, and decision-makers.

items.title: From 15 years old CMS to Drupal
items.full_description:
sara_rp
AuPairWorld

AuPairWorld's website launched in 1999 using a custom-built CMS called Acaio. For over 15 years, this remained their sole content management system. During that period, the site expanded to support six languages and hosted approximately 6,500 published pages.

Despite recognizing the platform's obsolescence, significant changes proved risky given their market leadership position, which included roughly one million monthly page impressions. In 2017, the organization decided to migrate to Drupal, beginning with a blog implementation before progressively adapting content types through paragraphs, modules, taxonomies, and views.

The implementation employed an agile methodology, allowing the team to refine content types iteratively. The speaker served as project coordinator and product owner, collaborating with IT and content teams. All involved parties transitioned from Drupal novices to experienced practitioners throughout the three-year journey.

This presentation shares the organization's migration project, lessons learned, and practical recommendations for similar transitions.

items.title: Welcome to the Era of Data Ownership
items.full_description:
Daniel Smidt, CTO at Synetic
Nick Veenhof, CTO at Dropsolid

The presenters examine how privacy regulations are reshaping the marketing technology landscape. They advocate for 'a move towards an open ecosystem that combines different Open Martech solutions into connected Digital Experience Platforms.'

Attendees will gain guidance on transitioning teams toward strategies centered on first-party data management in this evolving era. The session incorporates real-world case studies, practical field experience, and implementation strategies.

The speakers highlight how organizations can adopt open-source solutions including Mautic, Matomo, and Apache Unomi. These tools enable companies to maintain complete data control while preserving operational agility and maintaining service quality standards.

items.title: Successfully Managing Distributed Teams
items.full_description:
Stella Power
Annertech

Leadership presents inherent challenges, particularly during periods of crisis. The COVID-19 pandemic forced numerous organizations to transition to distributed operations rapidly, and many continue facing difficulties with project delivery and cultural maintenance.

Annertech brings '12 years experience of successfully operating as a fully remote, fully distributed team.' The session covers key topics including:

- Communication strategies that minimize excessive calls and meetings
- Building community and fostering belonging among remote staff
- Delivering projects efficiently while managing distributed teams
- Establishing boundaries that allow employees to disconnect

items.title: 4 years of Thunder: Why Hubert Burda Media went open source
items.full_description:
Daniel Bosen, juliapradel
Hubert Burda Media

Thunder represents one of Drupal's most widely adopted distributions. After operating for four years, the creators wanted to reflect on the journey's achievements and obstacles.

The German publishing organization Hubert Burda Media began developing a Drupal distribution in 2016 as an internal solution to handle an expanding business portfolio and changing needs. Since then, Thunder has powered many websites across various sectors beyond traditional media outlets, establishing itself as a primary distribution choice for professional publishing operations.

The presentation covers three main areas: the motivation to share their technology with not only competitors but with everyone who publishes content; the difficulties encountered throughout development and growth; and the positive outcomes achieved. The speakers emphasize their commitment to ongoing contributions to the Drupal ecosystem.

items.title: Drupal and Ansible: managing 2000+ environment infrastructure
items.full_description:
Mattias Michaux
Dropsolid

Dropsolid has developed a hosting platform designed to manage numerous environments and associated infrastructure components.

The platform evolved from 'a simple bash script to copy a site to a server' into a comprehensive system leveraging Drupal and Ansible as foundational technologies.

This technical presentation covers how the team integrated Drupal with Ansible, examines why these tools complement each other despite limitations, and addresses implementation challenges including single source of truth principles and reproducible test environments.

The speaker emphasizes this focuses on 'technical aspects and challenges encountered during the evolution of the platform' rather than marketing or competitive analysis.

items.title: Drupal and Gatsby: static without limits
items.full_description:
Oier Bravo

This presentation explores strategies for efficiently generating large numbers of static pages while maintaining an agile content editing experience. The speaker presents an approach for decoupling XXL sites that overcomes JSON:API limitations for streamlined Drupal data extraction and delivers an instant editing interface.

Key Achievements:
- Ultrafast compilation capabilities: approximately 100,000 pages compiled in 4 minutes; 1 million pages in under 30 minutes
- Cost-effective infrastructure for large-scale sites with monthly expenses below $1,000
- Ability to absorb traffic spikes without degradation
- Enhanced security posture

The session addresses Gatsby's advantages over traditional Drupal frontend implementations, creating dynamic features like sophisticated search functionality without incurring server costs, and Static Suite—a builder-agnostic Drupal module system featuring export capabilities via JSON, GraphQL, and JSON:API.

Attendees will understand how to decouple Drupal with Gatsby using CDNs to create secure, hardened sites; best practices for managing large static deployments; and serverless approaches for dynamic services.

items.title: Self-Management in remote environments
items.full_description:
Jorge Tutor

Management is an essential workplace tool, though we typically concentrate on team-management rather than self-management. The ability to manage oneself proves critical and often indicates your capacity to manage others.

'We all manage, and we all lead; these are not actions reserved for only those people who hold these positions' in organizations. Management applies broadly, not exclusively to managers, just as leadership extends beyond formal leaders.

Holding yourself accountable for work becomes increasingly crucial in remote work settings. This session covers acting with initiative and determination, intelligent self-organization, stress elimination, task prioritization, distraction removal, and creating space for original ideas.

Session Outline:
- Introduction
- Why be productive
- How to be productive: proactivity, perspective, simplicity, focus, method, self-control, evaluation
- Productive tools

items.title: Taking an Axe to your Pa11y
items.full_description:
Wouter Immerzeel, Tom Van Vliet

As demand for accessible websites is growing, the question arises how to make sure your site caters to all visitors.

In this session Tom and Wouter will talk about the how and why of accessibility as well as providing you with a toolset to make sure your next project will be a joy to use for everybody.

The presenters will discuss ensuring WCAG2.1 compliance, review tools for automated accessibility testing, and highlight common pitfalls you might encounter along with prevention strategies.

This session is designed for a broad audience—not only developers, but for anybody who needs to test the accessibility of websites. The content covers both automated testing of projects and manual evaluation methods.

items.title: My first Drupal Project as Junior PM
items.full_description:
akucherina

In March 2020, the speaker assumed their first role as Junior Project Manager on a Drupal initiative. The team developed a platform enabling people with Parkinson's disease and their support networks to safely share information.

Despite being new territory for many team members, the project succeeded. The speaker reflects on their experience through several lenses:

- Expectations versus reality in project management
- Which management responsibilities proved crucial versus anticipated
- Enjoyable aspects contrasted with challenging ones
- Key breakthrough moments and significant setbacks

items.title: Being Open about Being Human
items.full_description:
diego.f.costa

Mental health disorders affect millions globally and impact both employees and companies significantly. Despite this prevalence, stigma prevents many from discussing these challenges openly.

This presentation shares the speaker's personal experience with depression and anxiety. It aims to educate attendees about mental health conditions, identify warning signs, and introduce coping strategies that can help.

The session also highlights corporate initiatives designed to support employee mental wellness. These examples serve as potential models for organizations seeking to improve their own mental health support systems.

The overarching message emphasizes that being human at work—including acknowledging struggles—should be acceptable. The speaker demonstrates that vulnerability and openness in professional settings can yield surprisingly positive outcomes for individuals and organizations alike.

items.title: Control visibility with Entity visibility preview
items.full_description:
Florent Torregrosa

The presenter addresses a common challenge: displaying content differently based on user categories and managing content publication workflows. 'Have you ever needed to display contents or parts of a content differently depending on the user categorization?'

Several existing solutions exist, including custom project development, the scheduler module for node publication, and contributed modules like deploy. However, these primarily focus on nodes rather than other content types like paragraphs.

Torregrosa presents the Entity visibility preview module, developed at Smile, as a comprehensive solution to these issues. The presentation covers the underlying problem, the rationale for developing the module, and its functionality.

The session includes an introduction to the core challenge, explanation of why the Entity visibility preview module was created, a detailed module presentation, a live demonstration, and a question-and-answer segment.

items.title: Documentation: Why and how to do it now!
items.full_description:
qymanab

If someone were to join your team today, how quickly would they be able to ramp up? Would they be able to hit the ground running or would they keep tripping over the unspoken quirks of your system? Having documentation can solve many problems before they arise. Whether you are a team of one or one thousand, having a good, current reference of the whys and hows of your system can save you a lot of headaches down the line.

In this talk, the presenter discusses the benefits of having good docs and the potential risks and costs of the alternative; as well as tips and resources to get you started. Attendees will leave this session with:

- An overview of different types of documentation and their most effective use cases and audiences
- Techniques for writing and maintaining good documentation
- Arguments to get teams on board with making documentation part of their process

Documentation extends beyond the question of 'What does this code do?' As such, attendees of all levels and roles can benefit from this session.

items.title: Monitoring Kubernetes Drupal Clusters using Distributed Tracing
items.full_description:
Ricardo Amaro

This presentation addresses operators managing Drupal installations on Kubernetes infrastructure. Production cluster debugging can present significant challenges, including unplanned outages and operational overhead.

The session explores how distributed tracing 'uncovers how a lot of processes organize to deal with a singular user request.' Traditional tools like XHProf function adequately in monolithic systems, but Kubernetes environments demand modern alternatives including Zipkin, Jaeger, and Appdash.

Attendees will gain understanding of multiple tracing components: trace ingest and storage, application instrumentation, middleware configuration, distributed context propagation, and visualization retrieval systems.

Target Audience: Developers, systems administrators, and DevOps practitioners managing or planning Drupal deployments on distributed cluster infrastructure. Prior familiarity with Drupal on LAMP, cloud platforms, and Kubernetes best practices will enhance comprehension.

items.title: Multichannel publishing with content segmentation
items.full_description:
jurgenhaas

Drupal's content management capabilities are being extended beyond traditional online platforms into digital signage and out-of-home (DooH) marketing channels. This presentation explores how organizations can leverage a single content source across multiple distribution channels while maintaining editorial control.

The framework addresses a key business challenge: 'Avoiding content redundancies and keeping full control over editing and review processes, while utilizing high-end signage capabilities.' The speaker has developed an open source Digital Signage Framework compatible with Drupal 8 and 9, along with a plugin integrating signageOS—a major API-driven device management platform.

The presentation covers framework architecture, integration approaches with signageOS and other platforms, and real-world applications across industries including real estate. Implementation is already operational with European enterprise clients. The session concludes by examining future opportunities for the Drupal community within the digital signage ecosystem.

items.title: PHP 8: What's new and changing
items.full_description:
Ayesh

This presentation explores the innovations, modifications, and deprecations introduced in PHP 8, along with strategies for testing and migrating websites to this version. The speaker highlights major additions including Union Types, JIT compilation, Constructor Property Promotion, and Attributes.

The session also addresses significant removals of legacy functionality designed to eliminate outdated and potentially unsafe coding approaches. As the creator of PHP.Watch, the presenter provides insights into practical applications of new features and discusses breaking changes that could affect existing applications.

The talk emphasizes 'code samples' extensively. Presentation materials will be distributed beforehand, with printed copies provided during the session for attendee reference.

items.title: Decoupled translations with Drupal
items.full_description:
nbaosullivan

Gatsby is a popular static site generator that uses React, and it's a perfect match for a 'decoupled Drupal architecture to create lightning-fast websites.' This presentation explores how to leverage Drupal's multilingual capabilities to build a fully localized Gatsby site.

The session addresses setting up Gatsby for multilingual content sourced from Drupal and making Drupal aware of frontend interface translation strings, such as form labels or alert messages not available in Drupal for translation.

Attendees will discover how to create a multilingual Gatsby site with Drupal-sourced content, automatically synchronize translatable strings from Gatsby to Drupal, and understand key considerations for developing a translation management workflow.

Participants should have basic understanding of multilingual content and interface translations in Drupal.

items.title: Smart Paragraphs - Personalisation Engine for Nestlé
items.full_description:
Ashley Hazle, Lara Fernandes

The presenters collaborated with Nestlé Waters to develop a specialized module designed to customize content presentation based on data-driven triggers.

Recognizing broader industry demand, they partnered with Nestlé's global WebCMS team to expand their solution. This effort resulted in creating an innovative 'smart paragraphs' feature that works alongside existing block and segment modules within the Drupal ecosystem.

The session outlined how addressing Nestlé Waters' worldwide requirements informed a larger strategy for the global Nestlé web platform. Speakers documented the complete process from initial concept through submission as a Drupal community contribution, discussing the outcomes achieved.

items.title: A better Experience for Content Editors
items.full_description:
Sascha Eggenberger
Unic

The presenter explores strategies for configuring Drupal to enhance the content editing experience. Key contrib modules discussed include the Gin Admin Theme, Entity Reference with Layout, Paragraphs, core Layouts, Coffee, Field Groups, Media Library, Entity Browser, and Inline Entity Form variants.

The session covers practical setup instructions, configuration guidance, and code examples. Attendees receive access to a fully functional Drupal instance demonstrating these implementations. Special attention is given to the Gin admin theme, which builds upon Claro's foundation and incorporates design principles from the Amsterdam DrupalCon presentation on admin UI modernization.

Eggenberger serves as Senior UX Designer and Frontend Developer at Unic, previously holding the role of Lead Design and Frontend at Amazee Labs. He maintains several community projects and contributes to the Drupal Admin UI modernization Initiative. He also serves as a lead designer for the Drupal Design System.

items.title: TDD - Test Driven Drupal
items.full_description:
opdavies

Testing is important. It allows developers to add new features and modify existing code without concern for introducing regressions, reduces dependence on manual testing to identify bugs, and using a test-driven methodology results in leaner implementation code since you only write what is necessary for tests to pass.

Drupal 7 includes the SimpleTest module for unit and functional testing, while Drupal 8 supports PHPUnit—the standard PHP testing framework used by projects like Symfony and Laravel—making code testing more accessible. Testing serves as one of Drupal core's quality gates, with tests required for every new feature or bug fix and a 100% pass rate policy, making it an essential skill for core contributors and independent projects.

This presentation covers the methodology and terminology of automated testing, then demonstrates a test-driven approach to building a new Drupal module.

items.title: The Ten Ways of Trust
items.full_description:
trayevans

Putting trust at the core of your communications will help build better connections, better businesses, and better communities.

'Whatever matters to human beings, trust is the atmosphere in which it thrives.' - Sissela Bok, philosopher and ethicist

Trust plays an important role in values-based decision making. We need to be intentional about both the trust signals we consume and what we project in our communication.

In this talk, we'll explore why trust matters and cover ten practical tips to integrate trust elements into your communications.

Key Takeaways:
- Why trust matters
- Trust models
- Domains where trust matters most
- Trust & vibrancy signals
- Ten practical ways to build trust

items.title: What maintaining a large Drupal module is really like
items.full_description:
kristiaanvandeneynde

The session explores the realities of maintaining substantial Drupal modules. 'Without contribution, there would be no Drupal' and the framework depends on countless worldwide contributors building the ecosystem, particularly through modules available on drupal.org.

Drawing from seven and a half years of personal experience maintaining a large module, the presenter discusses challenges and rewards faced by module maintainers. The speaker has observed similar struggles among contributors to other major projects and core development.

The presentation aims to reveal what makes maintainership difficult while highlighting motivating factors that keep maintainers engaged. Several suggestions are offered to potentially ease the maintainer experience.

The speaker acknowledges that 'It's not all sunshine and rainbows in maintainerland' yet emphasizes the ongoing commitment to developing modules despite these challenges.

items.title: Drupal: Striving for Parity
items.full_description:
Vacilando

This presentation examines the practical considerations of pairing Drupal with GatsbyJS for building websites of varying complexity levels.

The speaker acknowledges that 'GatsbyJS is a modern open source JavaScript framework based on ReactJS, Webpack, JavaScript and CSS that allows developers quickly build very performant static websites and apps.'

While initial setup with Drupal as a backend data source takes only minutes, the presentation focuses on less-explored territory: scaling from simple sites to complex enterprise applications. The speaker explores how authentication, content previews, draft management, permissions handling, and build optimization become increasingly challenging as projects grow in scope.

The core argument posits that Drupal's strength lies in offering more functionality than simply serving as a backend. Through its extensive module ecosystem and robust API, Drupal can become a powerful data source for decoupled frontend applications like GatsbyJS, while also defining practical boundaries where traditional monolithic Drupal installations remain more advantageous.

items.title: Your Drupal Site Personalized Like Netflix
items.full_description:
prateekjain, bibliophileaxe

Drupal serves as the CMS for creating content-rich sites, yet 'displaying the same content to all users' is outdated. Modern websites must 'adapt to a wide range of users and their preferences.'

The presenters explain how Netflix's sophisticated personalization—though built on thousands of algorithms—breaks down into distinct, solvable use cases applicable to Drupal implementations using existing modules and technologies.

Session Flow:
- Why Personalize
- Understanding Netflix personalization use-cases
- Getting started with Personalization your Drupal solution
- Comparison of existing modules/technologies
- Solving Netflix like personalized use-cases in Drupal
- Applying modules to different use-cases
- Comparing different Drupal personalization modules for solving the same use-case

items.title: Streamline your development workflow with Lando and Lagoon
items.full_description:
pirog, Michael Schmid

Sponsored Talk at DrupalCon Europe 2020.

Two creators of popular open-source developer tools have partnered to integrate their platforms. 'The founders of two developer-favorite open-source web dev tools, Lando and Lagoon, have joined forces to bring the best of local Drupal development to Kubernetes.'

The presenters plan to discuss their new integrated solution for local development and deployment. They will showcase how developers can leverage this combination to enhance their workflows, share deployment optimization strategies, and explore emerging possibilities for Drupal development practices.

items.title: Build Healthy Multilingual Relationships
items.full_description:
aimeerae, penyaskito

As component-based design evolves, implementing these principles in Drupal involves many approaches. Most rely on entity relationships, but adding multilingual support that functions correctly and predictably presents challenges.

The session explores multiple entity relationship types: Paragraphs, Layout Builder, referenced nodes, custom entities, media entities, and taxonomy terms. Speakers address the complexity of nesting entities—blocks containing other blocks, which contain Paragraphs, taxonomy terms, and Media Entities within highly configurable components.

Multilingual implementation offers multiple configurations: translation versus localization, each requiring proper CMS and page display configuration for correct, predictable results—even with complex nested entities.

Topics Covered: Common multilingual configurations with entity nesting; considerations for component-based site-building architectures; existing community tools and potential future development needs.

items.title: Designing for chaos: Design process behind Olivero
items.full_description:
jwitkowski79, jponch

Olivero represents a core initiative to develop a new default theme for Drupal 9. Creating a theme for a core open-source project involves distinctive obstacles unlike those encountered when designing conventional websites.

This presentation explores the experience of developing a theme for an open-source content management system, addressing key topics including:

- The nature of Olivero and its creation rationale
- Obstacles specific to designing for an open-source community with thousands of participants
- Design decisions made to ensure broad accessibility
- The difficulty of creating themes for CMS platforms serving diverse website types
- Successful methodologies and processes employed

The speakers will guide attendees through practical techniques and workflows, examining each phase from initial conceptual mockups through abandoned design concepts that never reached implementation.

Participants will gain the ability to 'identify challenges, architect solutions, and validate results when designing a new theme for a content management system.'

items.title: How "Open" Applies to Marketing
items.full_description:
EricMFullerton

Everyone who uses Drupal believes in the concept of 'Open.' But for marketers, Open doesn't just mean open-source -- it means so much more.

In this session, the speaker will define how Open applies to doing better marketing, not only through using open-source technology but through an Open approach to integrations, APIs, machine learning, data, and much more. You'll learn what an Open approach to better marketing means, but you'll also hear examples and success stories of organizations who have adopted 'Open' concepts to their Marketing organization, and the impact they had.

items.title: Measuring search result quality
items.full_description:
Arra'di Rizal

This presentation examines methodologies for evaluating search quality effectiveness. Participants will learn practical approaches to assessing their search systems.

The content addresses three main areas:
1. The importance of quality measurement
2. Measurement approaches, including metric selection, necessary datasets, and establishing benchmarks for comparison
3. Implementation steps for building a measurement framework

The session explores real-world questions such as whether stopwords genuinely improve search outcomes and whether decomposing compound words enhances search performance.

The presenter has extensive experience as a Drupal developer since version 4.1 and has spent five years architecting and maintaining search infrastructure using Solr. Their expertise includes Information Retrieval systems integrated with various content management platforms, including Drupal.

items.title: Migrate to Drupal
items.full_description:
hussainweb

Drupal enables construction of intricate content frameworks, from basic blogs to complex enterprise publishing systems. This presentation addresses the migrate module, which offers a structured approach for transferring data into Drupal from multiple sources.

The session explores Drupal's migration capabilities for various content types, including upgrades from earlier Drupal versions. Since both Drupal 8 and 9 employ identical migration mechanisms for updates from versions 6 or 7, understanding migration development is essential as 'Drupal 7 EOL approaching soon and Drupal 9 release' makes this knowledge critical.

Learning Objectives: Participants will gain understanding of the migrate module and declarative programming approaches. The session covers migration planning, data restructuring, mapping strategies, code reuse through inheritance and traits, continuous migration, performance optimization, stakeholder auditing, and debugging techniques.

Key Takeaways: Attendees will learn migration concepts across both Drupal 7 and newer versions, discover tools that streamline the migration process, and develop skills to communicate migration details to stakeholders, write efficient migrations, and execute them effectively.

items.title: Privacy in 2020: Drupal Core Privacy Initiative
items.full_description:
Chris Teitzel

'From contact tracing to new regulations, privacy in the post COVID-19 world is going to look much different than it has before.'

The presentation examines how the changing privacy landscape, driven by emerging technologies and regulatory requirements, impacts the Drupal community. Teitzel discusses what measures the Drupal project is implementing to address privacy concerns.

The session includes a status update on the proposed core privacy initiative, followed by an open discussion and question-and-answer period about future directions.

Attendees are invited to participate in the conversation and contribute their perspectives on Drupal's role in protecting privacy within the open web ecosystem.

items.title: 4 Keys to Building Digital First Organization with Drupal
items.full_description:
EricMFullerton, mikemadison

Sponsored Talk at DrupalCon Europe 2020.

Today's organizations engage more frequently online across multiple channels than ever before. The pandemic accelerated the need for rapid adaptation, and those leveraging open source technologies like Drupal have positioned themselves as 'digital first' leaders.

This talk features stories from leading organizations that have utilized Drupal's power and flexibility to adapt, innovate, and improve online engagement. Presenters outline a technical roadmap for implementing similar approaches within your own organization.

Key technical topics covered include optimizing performance during traffic surges, implementing testing and DevOps pipelines for accelerated development cycles, establishing content workflows for efficient creation and management, and employing tools that integrate design, content, and customer lifecycle management.

items.title: What is between agencies and freelancing?
items.full_description:
Roland Molnar
Platform.sh

The speaker explores a middle ground between freelance work and traditional agency employment. He notes that while many creative professionals choose freelancing to escape rigid office schedules, this path quickly reveals limitations. Conversely, agencies struggle to maintain both productivity and quality while scaling.

The central question posed is whether one can combine the advantages of freelance flexibility with the structural benefits of an agency model. The speaker proposes a concept where independent contractors collaborate to form virtual creative studios.

Drawing from personal experience this year, he attempted this collaborative approach but ultimately transitioned to permanent employment. He plans to discuss both the challenges and benefits encountered.

With over two decades of professional experience, the speaker has held diverse roles including freelancer, agency owner, agency employee, product developer, and entrepreneur. His career has spanned technical positions (developer, architect) to business functions (sales, project management, product design). He currently works as a cloud engineer at Platform.sh.

items.title: Drupal is dead. Long live Drupal
items.full_description:
Kevin Bridges

With Drupal 9's release, the open source CMS entered a fresh phase in its evolution. The project has progressed significantly, navigating challenges and celebrating successes. Recent changes to Drupal's components and dependencies reflect the platform's maturation and future direction.

In the contemporary landscape, Drupal functions as one element within a broader ecosystem of services and tools required for modern project creation and deployment. Through collaboration with other open source initiatives, the community develops neutral best practices and software solutions that strengthen mutual support as the CMS continues evolving. Participants will gain perspective on the open source environment surrounding Drupal and discover avenues for active involvement.

The session addressed three primary areas: recent innovations in Drupal relative to broader open source initiatives, the Drupal community's positioning within 2020's open source discourse, and collaborative actions the ecosystem could undertake to foster advancement and growth.

items.title: Finding Answers to Your Drupal Questions
items.full_description:
Ashley Jones, Joe (eojthebrave)
Drupalize.Me

The session explores how to locate answers within the Drupal ecosystem. Presenters will guide attendees toward identifying which resources work best for different situations and maximizing their effectiveness when seeking help.

The discussion combines perspectives from someone new to Drupal (Ashley, a recent graduate of the Drupal Easy program) with someone who has deep experience (Joe, who has years of documentation and development background).

Learning Objectives: Attendees will gain the ability to locate Drupal answers, understand what support resources exist, navigate key platforms like drupal.org and api.drupal.org more effectively, and pose questions 'in a way that they are more likely to get a good answer.'

Target Audience: The session addresses newcomers wanting to learn about available resources, as well as experienced users seeking to use resources more efficiently and discover new options.

items.title: From squiggles to straight lines: Sketching UX
items.full_description:
Marissa Epstein
Lullabot

The core premise centers on sketching as 'a fast way to communicate intentions clearly, iteratively, and collaboratively' in UX and discovery processes.

Epstein draws from experience across design school and multiple career paths, emphasizing sketching's relevance for UX designers working on large-scale Drupal projects and other professional roles. She demonstrates how quick visual documentation can align project teams around shared understanding without requiring polished designs.

The presentation covers sketch-based tools and activities implemented at Lullabot, featuring real examples from recent user experience and strategy initiatives. Content addresses remote sketching techniques, in-person workshop approaches, and methods for digitally refining initial sketches.

Attendees will gain actionable takeaways, software recommendations, and strategies for integrating sketching into their workflows. The session welcomes beginners while providing intermediate-level content suitable for designers, strategists, project managers, product owners, and anyone seeking to document complexity visually and efficiently.

items.title: Taking Maximum Advantage of Drupal Core's Composer Template
items.full_description:
ultimike

For those developing a contemporary Drupal 8 or 9 installation, the Drupal core Composer 'recommended-project' template represents a logical choice. 'This modern, (officially) community-supported Composer template gets your project off on the right foot,' debuting with Drupal 8.8.

The presentation will break down this template's components and share practical strategies, advice, and techniques for maximizing its potential. The speaker will examine how it differs from the 'Drupal Composer / Drupal Project' alternative and introduce supplementary tools designed to streamline project management and code organization.

items.title: Tracking marketing lead journey with Drupal
items.full_description:
thimuth

When it comes to lead generation in sales and marketing, the website functions as a critical element in the customer journey, often serving as the initial point of contact with potential buyers. This presentation explores how to configure a Drupal website to monitor and manage each phase of the lead journey.

The marketing technology sector offers thousands of tools and solutions developed to integrate with websites and address various marketing needs. Both paid and free options exist for Drupal integration. Understanding available solutions is essential when implementing these integrations on a Drupal platform.

Beyond third-party integrations, custom Drupal implementations can track leads internally. This approach demands technical expertise, resources, and development time but provides greater flexibility and improved data analysis capabilities since you maintain control over stored information. However, developers must understand limitations imposed by data protection regulations including GDPR, CCPA, and LGPD.

The session subsequently addresses advantages and disadvantages of both approaches. The presenter discusses their organization's hybrid strategy, combining third-party tools with custom implementation, sharing practical insights from their experience.

items.title: Say no more than yes! XY problem
items.full_description:
nedsbeds

The conventional wisdom suggests 'Say yes more than no', yet this approach may not serve projects well when stakeholders present solutions rather than problems.

When gathering requirements, stakeholders frequently craft user stories that prescribe specific solutions instead of articulating underlying problems. This situation is termed an XY problem.

This presentation explores concrete instances of XY problems, techniques for recognizing them, and their potential to jeopardize software project success.

Attendees will learn to spot these problematic user stories. Rather than automatically agreeing, participants will discover methods to 'work out what will actually deliver value for your customers.'

items.title: Drupal initiative leads keynote
items.full_description:
Neil Drumm, Baddy Sonja Breidert, Gábor Hojtsy

Drupal's initiatives form powerful teams that make great things happen. Core initiatives self-organize to get new improvements to the base system while community initiatives coordinate event organization, spread diversity best practices, collaborate on promotional materials, and so on.

In the third installment of this keynote, attendees will hear from key leaders in the community about what they are working on, what their challenges are and how you can get involved.

items.title: "Flattening the Curve" with Lean Software Delivery
items.full_description:
Peleg Rabinowitz

The presentation addresses optimization challenges in software delivery processes. The speaker explores fundamental questions about identifying and classifying waste in operations, examining potential consequences and recommended responses.

The session documents a discovery journey undertaken to tackle process optimization at a Drupal agency managing multiple concurrent projects. The goal centers on achieving improved process control and stability while reducing inefficiency.

items.title: Driving today's CMS with tomorrow's artificial intelligence
items.full_description:
Jyoti Singh

The speaker explores how artificial intelligence and machine learning are increasingly relevant to content management systems, particularly Drupal. 'Artificial Intelligence and machine learning may seem as lingo in content management world but has made great inroads in this domain as well.'

For CMS platforms where personalization and adaptability matter, AI represents a potential transformative force. The presentation examines how machine learning concepts integrate with Drupal's ecosystem to enhance website capabilities and create more interactive user experiences.

The session covers several key areas: foundational concepts of AI and machine learning; business applications including sentiment analysis, entity analysis, topic segmentation, and language translation; AI integration within Drupal; Face APIs demonstrations; editorial experience innovations powered by AI; and practical applications of sentiment analysis for website monitoring.

items.title: Imposter Syndrome – it's way more common than you think
items.full_description:
aka_le_Mulder

The presenter explores how widespread imposter syndrome affects professionals in software development. Many IT workers experience feelings that they don't belong in their roles or deserve their compensation.

'There are two types of people – those who suffer from the Impostor syndrome and those who never heard of it.'

The session addresses how these feelings can lead to serious consequences including unexpected departures from positions, increased stress, and depression among talented engineers.

The presentation aims to examine this phenomenon in detail and offer practical strategies for individuals experiencing imposter syndrome to reduce its impact. Additionally, the speaker discusses how managers and colleagues can recognize when team members struggle with these feelings and provide meaningful support.

This session welcomes all attendees, particularly those who frequently feel misaligned with how others perceive them. No prior knowledge is required.

items.title: Load test your Drupal website before it is too late
items.full_description:
Janna Malikova

During times of crisis, governments and businesses depend on infrastructure to manage unexpected capacity demands and predictable traffic spikes. However, a Drupal application can sometimes be the source of problems. Website crashes due to unanticipated load are incidents no organization wants to experience.

This session addresses critical questions about Drupal performance:
- How many concurrent users can a Drupal application and its supporting infrastructure support before becoming unavailable?
- What methods exist to simulate load conditions for testing maximum capacity?
- Which monitoring tools effectively identify performance issues affecting applications?

Learning Objectives: The session provides foundational knowledge about load testing, including what it is and the different testing types available. Attendees will gain an overview of tools and services currently available, receive practical guidance for testing Drupal websites, and learn which environments support load testing.

items.title: Open personalization with Apache Unomi in GDPR era
items.full_description:
Nick_vh

The speaker addresses whether personalization remains viable in an era focused on consent, privacy, and GDPR compliance. He argues that 'Personalization doesn't have to be an Evil Big Brother' and emphasizes that when implemented with trust and consent, personalization effectively boosts engagement and user experience while improving conversion rates.

The session contrasts proprietary solutions with open-source alternatives. Rather than relying on external vendors who control customer data, the speaker advocates leveraging Drupal and Apache Solr to maintain complete data ownership. 'Drupal is yours to take. It is your responsibility to use it wisely.'

Apache Unomi is presented as a customer data management and personalization tool that, combined with Drupal and Mautic, creates a Digital Experience Platform without vendor lock-in. The approach maintains GDPR compliance while respecting user privacy.

The speaker demonstrates a fully decoupled architecture example using GraphQL for content delivery and React for rendering, while maintaining Drupal's core access systems and paragraph-based content structure.

Resources:
- Drupal Module: https://www.drupal.org/project/unomi
- PHP Library: https://gitlab.com/dropsolid/unomi-sdk-php
- JS Library: https://www.npmjs.com/package/unomi-sdk-node
- Documentation: https://unomi.apache.org/

items.title: Reactive Programming: Dealing with Asynchronicity
items.full_description:
tunic

This presentation introduces Reactive Programming via the ReactiveX library for JavaScript. The core concept involves 'declaring reactions to data change using data flows that transform data that crosses them.'

In JavaScript environments, much data is asynchronous—user interactions, Web Workers, server pushes from WebSockets, and AJAX calls all require management. While Promises improve upon callbacks, Observables and related Reactive Programming tools offer superior solutions by creating data pipes that clarify application behaviors. This approach produces 'shorter and meaningful code that is easier to understand than other approaches,' thereby enhancing maintainability.

Modern applications place significant logic on the client side, making Reactive Programming essential for complex applications with substantial data interrelation. RxJS is heavily integrated into Angular but can be adopted alongside React, Vue.js, or standalone implementations.

Intended Audience: Attendees should have experience building asynchronous applications or understand the challenges involved.

Learning Outcomes: Participants will grasp the fundamental principles of Reactive Programming and determine when to implement it in their projects.

items.title: The future of Elastic Stack from Drupal perspective (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on the future of Elastic Stack from a Drupal perspective.

Session Topics:
- SolR vs ES with regard to Drupal integration
- Contrib modules used and planned
- Integration of Elastic Site Search in Drupal
- Any other business on Search in Drupal

items.title: Building Frictionless Customer Journeys
items.full_description:
Leen Penders
Dropsolid

Every organization has the potential to enhance its customer experience significantly. Achieving frictionless customer journeys requires rethinking traditional approaches—visitors and customers navigate across multiple touchpoints rather than following predetermined funnels.

The presenter shares experience building visitor profiles beginning with the initial website interaction. This comprehensive data collection enables insights that support lead nurturing activities and deepen customer relationships.

This talk explores the speaker's journey as Chief Marketing Officer at Dropsolid, detailing the construction of personalized omnichannel experiences using exclusively open source solutions. The presentation addresses organizational obstacles encountered, the strategic methodology employed, valuable discoveries made, internal impact achieved, and measurable outcomes realized.

The session provides marketing professionals with practical knowledge regarding Drupal personalization capabilities, the Unomi customer data platform, and Mautic marketing automation functionality.

items.title: Documentation: A blueprint for effortless working!
items.full_description:
Vishal Khode

Documentation is frequently overlooked despite being 'an asset which conveys the Overall Vision & Care of a project.' Proper documentation maintains application records and enhances project quality.

New developer onboarding improves significantly with documentation, as team training on project specifics becomes more effective.

Pre-release documentation serves stakeholders by outlining product purposes and requirements while establishing realistic timelines for delivery.

Post-release documentation functions as a single source of truth, offering user manuals and reference guides that reduce dependency on informal knowledge within organizations.

The session explores why documentation matters beyond code alone, addresses barriers to writing documentation, and examines connections between documentation and code design quality. Topics include code reusability benefits and time/cost/effort savings for product owners, team members, and end users.

Learning Objectives: Attendees will develop proper work documentation skills, recognize technical knowledge documentation importance, and summarize workflows for complex tasks.

Target Audience: Project Managers and Product Owners seeking rapid developer integration.

items.title: LocalGov Drupal - UK councils openly collaborating on a Drupal distribution
items.full_description:
Finn Lewis

The LocalGov Drupal distribution aims to accelerate website development for UK councils using Drupal 9. With 408 councils across the UK spending substantial resources on publishing platforms, there is significant opportunity for shared solutions.

The initiative addresses common challenges including GDPR compliance, accessibility requirements, and emergency response needs. Approximately 60 councils already utilize Drupal and can contribute code and expertise to collaborative efforts.

Funded by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, participating councils are building a unified codebase. Rather than imposing uniform requirements, the team designs flexible components that serve diverse organizational needs.

Potential Benefits: The collaboration enables councils to reduce expenses, decrease development time, exchange best practices, and leverage innovations from peer organizations while enhancing public-facing digital experiences.

The presentation explores the project's evolution, motivations for collaboration and transparency, existing barriers, implementation strategies, current progress demonstration, future directions, and participation opportunities.

items.title: Moving Drupal forward by breathing new life into local community
items.full_description:
zeuty

This presentation examines the critical role local communities play in advancing Drupal's development and adoption. The speaker argues that leading or supporting a regional group carries equivalent importance to direct code or documentation work.

The session explores several key topics:
- Current state of Drupal's progress and trajectory
- Identifying the key drivers propelling the ecosystem forward
- Understanding potential risks and responsibility for addressing challenges
- How community definitions have evolved over time
- Practical guidance for establishing new local meetups
- Learning from thriving user group examples within the Drupal ecosystem

By the end of the session, participants will be equipped to assess their local community's health, plan their first meetup, and establish an official local community presence on drupal.org.

items.title: Seamless Drupal and Salesforce integration
items.full_description:
Joshua Li, Yavisht Katgara
Accenture

Accenture supported a major Australian government agency through digital transformation by integrating Drupal as the CMS and Salesforce as the CRM system. This unified approach delivered a consistent user experience across both platforms.

The presentation covered:
- Project background and context
- Selection rationale for both systems, including how Drupal was positioned
- Drupal architecture design approach
- Benefits of using a decoupled D8 architecture along with VueJS
- Integration technical challenges with code examples and visual aids
- Lessons learned and future implementation insights

items.title: Welcome to the party with Serverless One Stop Shop
items.full_description:
slootjes

The session explores a serverless architecture developed for Q-dance, described as 'one of the biggest organizers of events and festivals in the world.' The project demonstrates handling high-volume transactions, specifically 'selling 60.000 festival tickets within a few hours,' combined with multi-vendor product sales in a single transaction.

The technical implementation leverages AWS services including API Gateway, Lambda, Step Functions, IoT Core, Elasticache (Redis), S3, and SQS. A primary focus involves AWS Step Functions capabilities and their practical applications.

The solution enables users to purchase products from various affiliated vendors while completing payment only once through a unified platform. The session aims to inspire attendees regarding modern architecture approaches and demonstrate transferable solutions applicable to broader development projects.

items.title: Write better CSS using utility-first with Tailwind
items.full_description:
Phil Wolstenholme

CSS remains fundamental to web development, but implementing it effectively across large, multi-developer projects presents significant challenges.

Well-organized codebases often deteriorate over time as 'repetition, inconsistencies, and overrides-on-top-of-overrides' accumulate. Developers frequently hesitate to remove or modify CSS rules due to concerns about causing regressions.

Utility-first CSS methodology addresses these issues by relocating complexity and component definitions from stylesheets into markup—an approach well-suited to Drupal and Twig templates, though it requires a mindset shift.

This presentation explores the advantages of utility-first styling backed by over two years of client project experience. Topics include configuring Tailwind CSS alongside design systems, Twig templating techniques, relevant modules for component-based styling approaches, potential performance benefits, and improved developer experience.

items.title: Gin Admin Theme (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on the Gin Admin Theme.

Let's discuss about future settings, companion modules, your ideas etc.

items.title: Autosave and Concurrent editing in Drupal 8/9
items.full_description:
hchonov

This presentation focuses on two modules that enhance the editorial experience in Drupal 8/9: Autosave Form and Conflict.

The Autosave Form module protects against data loss by continuously saving the current state of entity forms. If unexpected disruptions occur, users can resume their work from the last saved version.

The Conflict module enables multiple users to edit identical content simultaneously. The system performs automatic merges when feasible. When incompatibilities arise, users receive visual tools to resolve them.

The talk examines both modules' current functionality and future development plans. It explores how they operate independently and the combined benefits of using them together. Since both are designed with customization in mind, the session provides technical insight into extending or modifying their capabilities.

items.title: Configuration Management Initiative 2.0
items.full_description:
Moshe Weitzman, Fabian Bircher

The configuration management initiative 2 achieved a significant milestone in Drupal 8.8 through a new API addition. While core development focused on releasing Drupal 9, the team worked on updating contributed modules to utilize the new core API.

With experience gained and Drupal 9 ready for fresh features, efforts have shifted back to enhancing the configuration management experience. This session covers the current state of the initiative, recommended practices for contributed projects, and opportunities for community involvement in advancing this work.

items.title: Content Architecture using Design Patterns
items.full_description:
adamjuran

Creating a solid content architecture in Drupal presents challenges due to numerous modeling possibilities. Common problems include excessive content types, overly complex field structures, and confusing naming conventions that harm both editorial and developer experiences.

The session draws parallels between web design evolution and content strategy. Modern design has shifted 'from being page-driven to being component-driven with Atomic Design being perhaps the most well known methodology.' Mapping these design patterns consistently to Drupal entities creates stronger architectures.

Success requires cross-functional collaboration among frontend developers, backend developers, solutions architects, and project managers. By combining component-based practices with rigorous data modeling, organizations can establish intuitive, reusable content structures that improve editorial workflows and developer satisfaction.

The presentation covers Atomic Design fundamentals, examines various component types with their frontend behaviors and content models, demonstrates template mapping to design patterns, and explores optimization strategies for content authoring experiences.

Target Audience: Solution architects, designers, frontend developers, Drupal site-builders, and site owners seeking to align design systems with content structure.

items.title: Drupal to power Open Data Platforms
items.full_description:
Patrick Beaucamp

This session introduces the Open Data challenge for governments and demonstrates how Drupal is implemented across multiple French governmental organizations to establish Open Data portals with sophisticated data visualization interfaces.

The presentation covers various 'Powered By Drupal' platforms in production, highlighting popular features including the data harvest process that enables connections to multiple OpenData platforms.

Participants will learn how users can create maps and charts within Drupal using Open Data databases. Production examples discussed include data.anfr.fr (featuring Node.js maps), data.infocom94.fr, agefma.data4citizen.com, and open.data4citizen.com.

items.title: Happier teams & clients with better PM
items.full_description:
ela.m, chipdavid
Cocomore

Cocomore faced persistent challenges managing projects effectively. The organization experienced inconsistency across project managers, shifting team composition throughout project lifecycles, and varying project scales.

These issues created problematic outcomes: 'people were overworked, we realized too late when things were not going as expected, risking either the deadline and/or the budget, and in the end work often was unnecessarily stressful.'

The speakers present their solution: a comprehensive restructuring of the PM department and establishment of standardized processes. Their framework includes defined Jira implementation protocols, team onboarding procedures, meeting cadences, and reusable templates.

Their core objective centers on achieving complete project visibility at all times, enabling superior planning capabilities. This approach ultimately delivers enhanced efficiency and reduced workplace stress for all stakeholders involved in projects.

items.title: Render me this... lazily
items.full_description:
joachim

Drupal 8 includes an advanced caching system designed to maximize page caching potential, even for pages mixing cacheable and non-cacheable content.

The session explores strategies for optimizing cache usage when building pages in controller classes. While designers and product owners determine page layout, developers can leverage caching mechanisms to improve performance.

Topics covered include custom caching approaches, lazy builders, custom token replacement in Twig templates, and additional optimization techniques.

items.title: Reverse Engineering Drupal Vulnerabilities
items.full_description:
mcdruid

This presentation examines actual Security Advisories from the Drupal Security Team, focusing on major vulnerability categories including Access bypass, Cross Site Scripting (XSS), SQL Injection (SQLi), and Remote Code Execution (RCE).

The speaker works backwards from each advisory to understand what vulnerabilities existed and how attackers could potentially exploit them. The session treats security analysis as an educational exercise designed to help attendees understand the Drupal Security Team's processes and better leverage their published information.

The goal is to help participants keep their Drupal sites secure by learning how the security review and disclosure process works.

items.title: Value Mapping: Communicating Benefits
items.full_description:
Jeffrey McGuire

This session focuses on developing clarity around an organization's offerings and their value proposition. Participants learn to construct what the presenter calls a Value Map—a collaborative tool for building consensus on core messaging.

The framework establishes 'agreed-upon language that everyone across all roles and departments can use to describe, position, write, and talk about your work consistently.' This shared vocabulary becomes a central reference point for various organizational functions.

The approach bridges technical and business perspectives. It enables engineering teams to understand how their implementation work connects to client outcomes. Simultaneously, it ensures marketing and sales departments communicate with confidence, knowing their messaging aligns with actual technical capabilities.

Practical Applications: The Value Map supports multiple business functions including marketing strategy development, content creation, technical roadmap prioritization, competitive analysis, and information architecture planning.

items.title: Decoupled Menu Initiative (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on the Decoupled Menu Initiative.

At DrupalCon Global 2020, Dries introduced a new initiative focused on developing a decoupled menu component using JavaScript. To maintain Drupal's framework-neutral approach, the proposal includes creating components compatible with both Vue.js and React.js.

This Birds of a Feather session welcomes anyone interested in contributing to this initiative.

items.title: Drupal in microservices and Kubernetes (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on Drupal in the world of microservices and Kubernetes.

This session serves as a follow-up to the DevOps presentation covering 'Drupal Distributed Tracing and Kubernetes' held on Tuesday.

The BoF functions as 'an open forum meant to raise questions and answers for the future of Drupal as a microservice component in the world of Kubernetes.'

items.title: Community managers and enthusiasts (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session for Drupal Community Managers, Ambassadors, and enthusiasts.

The session invites Drupal Community Managers, Ambassadors, and enthusiasts to participate in a discussion forum. Attendees are encouraged to 'Come for the code, stay for the community.'

The gathering focuses on sharing experiences and insights accumulated over the previous year, particularly considering the challenges posed by pandemic-related circumstances. Participants will exchange learnings and discuss strategies for sustaining community growth into 2021 and beyond.

items.title: Empowering African woman in tech
items.full_description:
Ada Nduka Oyom
She Code Africa

This presentation examines how She Code Africa, a nonprofit operating across the continent, is strengthening Africa's tech sector by closing gender disparities and enabling women and girls to enter technology fields or expand their technical abilities through free resources.

Ada founded She Code Africa in 2016 as a nonprofit dedicated to advancing young women and girls through technical education. The organization has reached 'over 5000 women members across 15 African countries' and promotes diversity within technology sectors.

Ada began her career as a self-taught software developer during university and has since held positions with multiple African tech organizations. Her developer advocacy work earned her appointments with major global companies, including her role as Ecosystem Community Manager for Sub-Saharan Africa at Google.

She co-founded Open Source Community Africa, a major regional hub for open-source professionals. Ada hosts the Forloop pod podcast featuring technical discussions and expert interviews. She mentors aspiring tech professionals and has received recognition including Ytech 100 honors and TechWomen of Lagos designations.

items.title: Creating more value with Drupal as DXP
items.full_description:
Dominique De Cooman
Dropsolid

According to Gartner, '93% of customer experience projects yield return on investment.' Forward-thinking organizations are transitioning from individual Drupal websites toward digital experience platforms (DXP).

This presentation explores how Drupal can function as a digital experience platform. Attendees will understand the distinctions between conventional websites and DXP solutions. Enterprise participants will discover how digital experience platforms facilitate digital transformation initiatives and boost customer lifetime values.

The content targets enterprises exploring Drupal for digital transformation and Drupal service providers interested in marketing Drupal as an open DXP alternative to proprietary solutions like Adobe, Sitecore, or Bloomreach.

With 13 years of expertise in digital customer experiences using Drupal, the speaker has supported hundreds of organizations with open digital experiences and transformation efforts. Dropsolid, founded in 2013, expanded to 65 employees within five years due to rising demand for open digital customer experiences (DCX).

items.title: Configuration Management for Beginners
items.full_description:
davidneedham

This presentation addresses a common challenge in Drupal development: moving database-stored configuration from development to production environments safely and efficiently.

The speaker explains that while code deployment via Git is straightforward, configuration changes like content types, fields, and views require careful management. Rather than recreating these elements in live environments, the session teaches participants how to extract configuration from the database and maintain it in version control.

Key Learning Outcomes: Attendees will master several competencies by the end of the session. They'll implement comprehensive workflows for site building, migrate configuration from databases into version control systems, import settings through both user interfaces and command-line tools, automate imports across multiple environments, and enhance team development processes.

Intended Audience: The content targets three primary groups: organizations requiring zero-tolerance policies for deployment errors, site builders seeking rapid live environment updates, and teams wanting configuration versioning with change tracking and accountability.

Prerequisites: Basic Drupal site building knowledge and familiarity with best practices are recommended. However, prior experience with version control, configuration management, or command-line interfaces is optional.

items.title: Enterprise grade editorial experience
items.full_description:
breidert
1xINTERNET

The approach to constructing CMS platforms has evolved significantly. Modern systems now separate frontends from backends, making the editorial interface a crucial factor in CMS selection.

Contemporary editors expect to work directly within frontend environments using WYSIWYG tools, rather than solely operating within structured backend systems.

1xINTERNET created modules designed to enhance the editorial workflow. One enables content reuse through entity templates with an interface comparable to Google Docs. Another in-development module permits frontend editing of entities directly.

These modules leverage Drupal's API architecture while maintaining lightweight integration that supports extension. Both are planned for contribution to the community.

The presentation will cover:
- Defining enterprise-level editorial experience
- Template module functionality and workflow integration
- Frontend editing capabilities and API utilization

Participants will learn how to enhance editorial experiences, identify features requested by editorial teams, and understand what constitutes professional-grade editorial interfaces in modern CMS environments.

items.title: My best (and worst) strategies for high-demand work
items.full_description:
Michael Schmid
Amazee

Across various roles and companies, job stress continues to rise. The constant stream of emails, messages, and urgent tasks creates overwhelming conditions that can lead to burnout.

As CTO of Amazee, Michael Schmid manages a globally distributed team operating 24/7. Over the past decade, he has experimented with numerous approaches to manage high-demand work environments. Some strategies proved effective while others did not.

The speaker will share personal experiences and practical techniques covering:
- Sleep improvement and faster sleep onset
- Managing notification overload
- Daily structure and organization
- Weekly self-reflection practices

Attendees will gain specific, implementable stress-reduction strategies and learn to develop personalized plans for their situations. The session emphasizes preventing burnout and facilitates peer discussion among those navigating similar challenges.

items.title: Open source has won - how do we avoid dying of success? (Panel)
items.full_description:
Baddy Sonja Breidert, Cristina Chumillas, Eriol Fox

This panel discussion brings together project maintainers, users, business owners, and other open source community stakeholders to examine the future of the ecosystem. Participants explore the challenges facing different roles within the community and identify collective actions to ensure the sector remains equitable and sustainable.

The panel addresses three primary topics: Each speaker provides an introduction and shares their perspective on open source's current state, followed by discussion exploring what it means that 'open source has won' in the technology landscape.

The group examines sustainability questions, including concerns about corporate entities that benefit from OSS projects without contribution, the demographic composition of contributor communities, and whether projects can better appeal to younger or more diverse participants. The discussion also considers whether expanding user diversity strengthens the ecosystem.

The session includes audience question-and-answer time.

items.title: Overview of Drupal front-end component integration methods
items.full_description:
Brian Perry

Since Drupal 8's release, significant progress has been made developing component-based theming that leverages Twig and integrates with component libraries and design systems. This approach reduces redundant code by allowing Drupal and tools like Pattern Lab or Storybook to 'share the exact same code.'

However, coordinating data mapping between Drupal and external component libraries remains challenging for larger teams.

This session covers multiple methods for passing data from Drupal to front-end components outside traditional template directories, including:
- Data mapping via preprocessing and Twig templates
- Helper modules (Component Libraries, Twig Tweak, Twig Field Value)
- Component-based themes and starter kits
- UI Patterns and supporting modules
- Pattern Kit, Compony, and Single File Components

The presentation also explores how this workflow could evolve in future Drupal versions.

Attendees will learn to develop solutions for mapping Drupal data to external components, recognize integration challenges, and identify approaches best suited to their team or project needs.

items.title: QA Automation: Removing repetitive tasks while giving real value
items.full_description:
BiancaM, david.pvb

The presenters address a common challenge in Drupal projects: reducing quality assurance hours to allow teams to focus on more valuable business activities. They developed an automation solution for the QA process.

The automation primarily targets Drupal security updates, core updates, and features affecting multiple sites. The approach divides test automation into two packages: one covering 'User stories, JS & SEO test automation' and another handling 'Visual regression & performance test automation.' These differ in their tools and testing frequency.

The speakers showcase a successful implementation using a Drupal 8 multisite architecture for Nestlé. Built on Acquia Lightning, the system manages 12 different sites. The QA automation integrates seamlessly into the project structure while aligning with Nestlé's Digital Transformation Services department.

items.title: Upgrading to CKEditor5 (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on upgrading to CKEditor5 in Drupal core.

CKEditor is an important part of Drupal core, and upgrading to the latest CKEditor5 was identified as a key Drupal 10 readiness initiative. CKEditor5 includes exciting new features that could dramatically improve the D10 authoring experience.

This Birds of a Feather session welcomes both contributors and those seeking to learn more about the initiative.

items.title: Open Source & Return on Experience for mid-market
items.full_description:
Frederic De Vries, Anneleen Demasure

The presenters explore foundational concepts around open source philosophy and its business applications. They examine 'Return on Experience' as a framework, discussing its core principles and operational mechanisms.

The session addresses how organizations can evaluate customer behavior changes through this lens. Presenters explain measurement approaches, distinguishing between 'Return on Experience' and traditional ROI metrics, while outlining implementation strategies.

They discuss improvement triggers and obstacles organizations face when integrating these concepts. The speakers propose establishing comprehensive plans similar to traditional marketing frameworks at mid-sized enterprises.

The session concludes by demonstrating how combining open source principles with experience-focused strategies can secure executive leadership support. This approach enables organizations to assess digital transformation initiatives based on 'value and not on their cost.'

items.title: Driesnote
items.full_description:
Dries Buytaert
