During his keynote at DrupalCon Europe 2020, Dries presents an engaging address regarding the state of the Drupal project. The Belgium-born Drupal founder is recognized as 'a pioneer in the open source web publishing and digital experience platform space.'

items.title: Core Automatic Updates Initiative Update
items.full_description:
tedbow, heddn

During Drupal Global, Dries unveiled Automatic Updates as one of five key strategic priorities for Drupal 9. This initiative builds upon existing work that produced a contributed module offering updates for non-Composer-based Drupal 7 and 8 sites.

The next phase aims to extend support to Composer-based sites targeting Drupal 9. The team is currently focused on 'moving update readiness checks and other supporting functionality from the contributed module into Drupal core.'

By the Barcelona conference, organizers anticipated presenting a work-in-progress demonstration of Composer-based automatic updates functionality.

items.title: D7 & D8 End of Life in 2021
items.full_description:
Michael E. Meyers, Jeremy (Tag1)

Over one million websites depend on Drupal 7 and D8, both reaching end of life in 2022 (extended from the original 2021 deadline). Site owners face challenges regarding upgrade paths, particularly for D7, prompting critical questions about timelines and available alternatives.

Upon reaching EOL, automated testing, official releases, bug fixes, and security patches will cease. Organizations can maintain secure operations through paid commercial support via Drupal 7 Vendor Extended Support (D7ES), authorized through select vendors including Tag1.

This program explores what EOL means for Drupal and dependent software like PHP and Symfony. Attendees learn about available options, including Vendor Extended Support capabilities and whether these solutions offer temporary relief or long-term viability.

Key Topics Covered: The session addresses why major versions reach EOL, impacts on dependent technologies, available mitigation strategies, and timelines before the deadline arrives.

Target Audience: Anyone currently managing Drupal 7 or D8 sites expected to operate beyond 2021. No technical prerequisites required.

items.title: Drupal Agency Partnerships: Stronger, Together
items.full_description:
Nathan Roach, Piyush Poddar

The Drupal agency sector continues to evolve, presenting new challenges in the post-pandemic environment. This session examines current data regarding the state of Drupal business within agencies, incorporating insights from agency leadership perspectives.

The presenters explore emerging opportunities for collaboration within an industry traditionally characterized by competitive dynamics. They highlight how 'symbiotic opportunities both new and exciting' can help agencies work more effectively together and strengthen the overall ecosystem.

The discussion focuses on identifying practical approaches for agencies to improve their collective position and build stronger partnerships, addressing the challenging business terrain many Drupal agencies face in the current market landscape.

items.title: Drupal.org Update panel
items.full_description:
hestenet, rachel_norfolk, Neil Drumm, Ryan Aslett

The Drupal.org Update panel maintains a 'bi-annual tradition of updates on the work of the Drupal Association Engineering team, and the future of the tools and systems that the Drupal Community use to build Drupal.'

This session covered several key topics:
- An update on Merge Requests using Drupal.org's issue queue integration
- A discussion of the future of DrupalCI
- Lessons learned from the DrupalSpoons initiative and how to apply them to Drupal.org
- Drupal 10 readiness and its implications for Drupal.org
- Community support strategies while managing the migration to Drupal 9

items.title: Drupal Local Development AMA (BoF)
items.full_description:
Randy Fay (Maintainer of DDEV-Local) and maintainers of other tools

Randy Fay and fellow maintainers of local development tools will facilitate an informal discussion session. Participants can raise any questions related to local development work. The session welcomes 'any question' on topics within this domain. Organizers indicated the group could potentially 'work together on shared screens' if that approach proves beneficial for addressing attendees' needs.

items.title: Improve Drupal Commerce visibility (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on improving Drupal Commerce visibility.

Drupal Commerce lacks visibility compared to other eCommerce solutions. Key issues include:
- The Drupalcommerce.org website is outdated
- The showcase lacks current relevance
- Marketing materials such as brochures and press releases are unavailable

The session's primary focus centers on collaborative problem-solving: identifying strategies to create promotional tools and resources that would enhance Drupal Commerce's visibility within the broader eCommerce ecosystem.

items.title: MongoDB on D9+ (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on what should be next for MongoDB on D9+.

The MongoDB modules have existed since Drupal 6 and have undergone significant evolution. While these modules now benefit from 'better support on D9 than they ever had,' their community footprint has become notably smaller.

As Drupal technology choices continue to shift through versions 9 and 10, this Birds of a Feather session explores potential pathways forward. Participants will discuss how the MongoDB project could become more valuable to the Drupal ecosystem and what strategic directions contributors should prioritize.

items.title: Caching and performance deep dive 2.0 (Workshop)
items.full_description:
Fabian Franz

Drupal features an advanced caching system with significant optimization opportunities. This workshop builds on a successful 2020 session, providing hands-on learning through practical exercises. Participants are encouraged to bring laptops for interactive participation.

The session covers fundamental caching concepts including what to cache, where caching occurs, and common pitfalls. New content addresses creating custom cache bins, real-world cache context examples, decoupled Drupal implementations, and placeholder strategies.

Advanced topics include authenticated user caching techniques and edge content delivery network integration—the most requested topic from the previous workshop.

Key Learning Outcomes: Attendees will gain ability to manually cache content, understand cache invalidation and variation, apply caching principles across contexts, and solve performance challenges in Drupal 8, including placeholder and authenticated user caching scenarios.

Prerequisites: Participants need basic PHP and Drupal 8 knowledge, plus ability to install, run, and modify sites using drush.

Fabian architected major components of Drupal's caching system. He advocates empowering the community to fully realize the system's potential.

items.title: Retrospective: COVID-19 crisis impact on client relationships (Workshop)
items.full_description:
Josef Kruckenberg, Joanita Bonnier, Steve Holyer

This interactive workshop targets professionals working in open source delivery and customer-facing roles. The facilitators, described as 'a team of agile coaches,' guide participants through a retrospective format to examine how the pandemic influenced their work and relationships.

The session employs a structured retrospective approach where attendees 'share and learn from our experiences with the COVID-19 crisis.' The workshop combines two elements: celebrating successes achieved during the crisis period and identifying lessons that can inform future improvements.

Participants interested in attending were directed to complete a sign-up survey form to secure their spot in this facilitated workshop experience.

items.title: Your first steps to successful content strategy (Workshop)
items.full_description:
Baddy Sonja Breidert

Every web project requires foundational elements: content strategy with goals, user experience and design, plus thoughtfully structured information architecture within a CMS system.

These responsibilities typically fall to different specialists: content strategists, analytics professionals, UX and graphic designers, accessibility experts, solution architects, and developers.

The core challenge involves 'creating a mutual understanding of all stakeholders and an easy to understand workflow for people to collaborate.'

The presenter's company developed a ten-step workflow model applied across all projects:
1. Define business goals
2. Create a content strategy
3. Segment website user audience
4. Plan user journeys and content personalisation
5. Create UX and site structure
6. Create Design and Frontend
7. Create Backend (CMS)
8. Create content
9. Setup tracking
10. Run monthly analysis on websites

During this workshop, the speaker covers the first four steps with practical examples and shareable templates for participants to use in future projects.

items.title: Advanced front-end debugging techniques for back-end developers
items.full_description:
Anna Mykhailova

Different browsers, various devices, multiple screens, fast-evolving technologies and ever changing CSS properties comprise the daily reality of front-end development. This presentation addresses back-end developers seeking to strengthen their debugging capabilities, full-stack professionals wanting to enhance their workflow, and front-end specialists validating their approaches.

The session begins with browser development tools, then explores helpful extensions and external services. Participants will learn on-device debugging across multiple browsers and platforms to address a central front-end challenge: 'Why my CSS/JS isn't doing what I expect it to do?'

Attendees are encouraged to bring laptops and select a preferred site and browser to follow along with real-world examples demonstrating practical debugging solutions.

items.title: Driesnote Q&A panel
items.full_description:
Dries Buytaert, Drupal Project Founder
Heather Rocker, Drupal Association Executive Director

Attendees had the opportunity to engage with leadership about the Driesnote presentation and the future direction of the Drupal Project. The panelists fielded inquiries from session participants, who could 'submit their questions via the OnAir platform during the session.'

items.title: Leading through Uncertainty
items.full_description:
jmcwherter

The speaker addresses everyday business uncertainties including client reactions to constraints, employee performance, and contract sourcing. Drawing on leadership experience, the presenter notes that 'It is possible to commit no mistakes and still lose, because there is always uncertainty.'

The talk focuses on practical strategies for managing uncertainty through organizational practices. Key themes include fostering honesty and transparency within teams, as well as developing approaches to motivate and inspire staff members. The speaker contends that how leaders handle uncertainty—rather than eliminating it—can determine business success.

items.title: The highs and lows of Community Leadership
items.full_description:
Tara King, Yan Zhang, Tearnye Almendariz

Open source communities bring together people from various backgrounds and disciplines. As efforts continue toward making these communities more inclusive, a significant focus involves empowering underrepresented and marginalized individuals to assume leadership roles.

The presenter received leadership of Drupal's volunteer-driven diversity initiative, the Drupal Diversity & Inclusion working group, in 2018. This transition sparked intensive learning about adaptation, adjustment, and establishing a personal leadership direction. The DD&I group aims to develop a more inclusive Drupal community through varied initiatives. As a young Muslim woman leading this effort, the speaker encountered substantial challenges.

Leadership demands included articulating a team vision, establishing collective objectives, engaging with established community power structures, and implementing meaningful work supporting marginalized community members. These responsibilities presented multifaceted obstacles.

This presentation shares lessons acquired through that experience and offers strategies intended for aspiring community leaders.

items.title: Alternative DrupalCI using Docker containers (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on an alternative for DrupalCI using Docker containers.

The presenter addresses a common challenge: 'To run DrupalCI locally you need to install a lot of things and its not straight forward for most users.'

The session showcases a functional prototype enabling local development and testing of contributed modules for Drupal versions 7, 8, and 9 using a single command. The prototype also demonstrates integration methods for Jenkins job implementation.

items.title: Best practices in moving and deploying sites (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on best practices in moving and deploying sites.

The session focuses on practical strategies for site migration and deployment activities. 'We all have to move or deploy sites from time to time.'

The discussion covers multiple migration scenarios, including transferring sites between servers, switching hosting providers, moving production environments to local development setups, and pushing development instances to production. Participants are invited to share and learn optimal procedures for these common site management tasks.

items.title: Drupal Accessibility (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on Drupal accessibility.

Discussion about Drupal, accessibility, open source and how we can continue on the accessibility journey.

items.title: Automatic Updates Initiative Feedback (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on the Drupal Core Automatic Updates Initiative.

This was an open Birds of a Feather session welcoming anyone interested in the Automatic Updates Initiative. Participants were invited to 'discuss the initiative' with all community members encouraged to attend.

The session aimed to cover multiple aspects of the project, including reactions to user experience design mockups, the PHP-TUF library and Update Framework implementation, necessary Composer plugins, relevant Drupal core issues, and practical considerations affecting real-world update deployment scenarios.

items.title: Keynote: Centring humans and their rights in Open Source Design
items.full_description:
Eriol Fox
Open Food Network; Open Source Design core team; Human Rights Centred Design working group

Eriol Fox has spent a decade designing solutions for complex challenges. Their experience spans for-profits and then moving into NGOs and open source software organisations, working on complex problems like sustainable food systems, peace building and crisis response technology.

Fox currently contributes to multiple initiatives focused on ethical design practice. They serve as part of leadership at Open Source Design and the Human Rights Centred Design working group.

This keynote explores centring humans and their rights in open source design practice.

items.title: Adding starterkit theme to Drupal core (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on adding a starterkit theme to Drupal core.

The organizers aim to introduce a new starterkit theme into Drupal core that would serve as a replacement for Classy in the future. This Birds of a Feather session focuses on collaborative planning and discussion regarding the implementation roadmap and next steps for the initiative.

items.title: Gin Admin Theme (BoF)
items.full_description:
saschaeggi

BoF session on the Gin Admin Theme at DrupalCon Europe 2020.

items.title: Online Drupal events in 2021 (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on online Drupal events in 2021.

Given the arrival of COVID vaccines alongside persistent uncertainty about in-person gatherings, the event industry faces significant challenges. This session addresses critical questions facing the Drupal community.

Key topics for discussion include whether organizing local camps remains viable, whether virtual formats prove sufficiently effective, and how to maintain financial viability. The session invites participants to share perspectives and ideas on these pressing matters affecting Drupal's event landscape in the coming year.

items.title: Solr versus Elasticsearch
items.full_description:
Valerie Valkenburg-Gibson

Although both search engines derive from the same Lucene technology foundation, ongoing tension exists between these two platforms. The speaker examines why conflict often appears driven by emotion rather than objective analysis.

The presentation addresses key decision-making factors: What leads organizations to select one system over another? Are stakeholders satisfied with their chosen implementations after deployment?

The session offers a systematic comparison using complex datasets and results analysis. It evaluates three critical dimensions: 'performance, user-friendliness and reliable search results.' The speaker positions this as 'the mother of all search shootouts,' providing a comprehensive evaluation framework for practitioners choosing between these search engine options.

items.title: Content Delivery of Tomorrow
items.full_description:
Archita Arora, Ruchika Mohite

Over recent years, Drupal has evolved beyond a traditional CMS platform to become a comprehensive Digital Experience Platform. Marketing professionals constantly seek to deliver contextual, targeted content that provides genuine value to users. Drupal streamlines this process, enabling faster and more effective content distribution.

This presentation explores the intersection of content and user experience, demonstrating how Drupal empowers content writers to accelerate their publishing workflows. The speakers share real-world case studies highlighting organizations that leveraged Drupal within their marketing operations to establish sustainable competitive advantages.

Target Audience: Content creators, marketers, content strategists, site owners, and designers working with Drupal-based websites.

items.title: Designing for Hidden Persona
items.full_description:
Jacob Bell, Meaghan Shanley, Tim Senft
Jon.ZenSource

The presentation addresses a frequently overlooked design consideration: content authors themselves. 'Success is reliant on an author's ability to use Drupal to transform content strategy into a marketing engine.'

The session explores how organizations often prioritize technical implementation while neglecting the business and user experience dimensions, particularly regarding content organization and strategy.

Drawing from experience with diverse clients in healthcare and higher education, the speakers present a three-part framework:

Content Strategy & Planning involves initiating planning from project inception, establishing checkpoints, and aligning strategy with the Drupal ecosystem through module mapping and taxonomy work.

Product Playbook focuses on developing a comprehensive Drupal implementation approach tailored to how content authors actually work, including iterative releases and customized page templates.

Technical Process to Optimize the Admin covers Drupal module selection and customization techniques designed specifically for author workflows.

Key takeaways include understanding how to design Drupal for content authors, implementing new processes for creation and planning phases, and adopting test-and-learn approaches for the authoring experience.

items.title: How to train the dragon
items.full_description:
gargsuchi
Accenture

The speaker addresses the challenge of recruiting skilled Drupal professionals, noting that 'great Drupal talent is even harder to come by.' As a newer entrant to Australia's Drupal market, Accenture faced difficulties attracting local talent through traditional agency channels.

To build a sustainable workforce, Accenture developed an internal graduate training initiative. This program develops junior talent inhouse, creating a reliable pipeline of qualified Drupal professionals. The program combines classroom instruction with hands-on project work, allowing graduates to gain practical experience while contributing to real client deliverables.

The speaker plans to discuss the graduate program's structure, implementation strategies, and how trainees transition into meaningful project roles. Additionally, the presentation covers potential challenges and pitfalls inherent to this training approach, offering recommendations for avoiding common obstacles when establishing similar programs.

items.title: Low code, past, present and future
items.full_description:
Alejandro Moreno Lopez

The technology sector faces significant recruitment challenges, with developer demand substantially outpacing supply. While this situation might initially appear favorable for IT professionals, underlying concerns warrant closer examination.

Educational reforms alone cannot address immediate workforce shortages. Instead, the industry requires improved development tools to bridge the gap between current demand and available talent. A growing ecosystem of solutions—from major cloud providers like Google and Amazon to emerging startups and open source initiatives—aims to democratize software development capabilities.

Even established platforms are adopting low-code approaches. 'See Gutenberg in Wordpress or Layout Builder in Drupal' as examples of this shift toward user-friendly interfaces.

This presentation explores the evolution of low-code and no-code technologies, examines current market trends and available solutions, discusses Drupal integration possibilities, and analyzes future industry direction. The speaker invites discussion on whether these tools represent a threat or opportunity for content management systems like Drupal, WordPress, and Joomla.

items.title: Sustainable practices for building and maintaining Open Web (Panel)
items.full_description:
Josef Kruckenberg, Philipp Melab, Laura Gaetano

The digital landscape continuously shifts, and web-based solutions regularly encounter the challenge of becoming obsolete. Technical debt frequently impedes forward progress and innovation.

This panel brings together Open Web creators to explore sustainable approaches to web development. Participants will discuss the methods these experts employ to construct web solutions that endure and adapt to changing market demands throughout their lifecycles.

Previous panel discussions from DrupalCon Amsterdam 2019 and DrupalEurope serve as references for the discussion format and caliber.

items.title: Add end to end tests with CypressIO
items.full_description:
fjgarlin

This presentation demonstrates how to integrate CypressIO testing into an existing Drupal site quickly. The speaker conducts a live demonstration covering the practical steps needed to add end-to-end tests to Drupal projects.

Key Topics Covered:
- Drupal 7 integration
- Drupal 8 integration
- Writing initial tests
- Next steps for implementation

Attendees unfamiliar with Cypress integration will gain the knowledge and skills to 'include Cypress into their projects' by the session's conclusion.

items.title: Containerisation of Mautic Application
items.full_description:
Sreekar Achanta

This presentation addresses scalability and maintenance challenges faced by Mautic users during intensive marketing campaigns. The speaker explores how the open-source marketing platform wasn't initially enterprise-ready or aligned with cloud-native principles.

Key Issues Addressed: The session highlights several architectural problems: the application wasn't designed following '12 Factor Application philosophy,' contained multiple configuration files for environment variables, and the official Docker image wasn't optimized for Kubernetes deployment. Additionally, ephemeral and persistent components weren't properly separated, and the container ran multiple processes simultaneously—considered an anti-pattern in containerization.

Learning Outcomes: Attendees will discover how the team redesigned the application architecture, decoupled components using native Kubernetes services, streamlined Docker image updates, consolidated configurations into a single config.php file, and implemented security best practices aligned with cloud-native methodologies.

Impact: The containerized, orchestrated solution transformed deployment processes from virtual machines and manual procedures to frequent, automated releases. The combination of Kubernetes' self-healing capabilities and AWS auto-scaling features created a highly resilient system, while GitLab CI/CD pipelines simplified developer workflows.

items.title: Building platform to Celebrate Drupal
items.full_description:
dan2k3k4

This presentation documents the creation of CelebrateDrupal.org, covering multiple aspects of the platform's development.

The speaker explores design decisions informed by the Olivero frontend theme, detailing how visual inspiration was incorporated into the site's appearance.

Development work centered on building a Drupal 9 site prior to that version's official release.

Marketing efforts focused on community engagement, particularly in gathering user-submitted images and videos for the platform.

Content management involved overseeing the moderation queue to maintain quality contributions.

The speaker adapted the platform's functionality during DrupalCon Global Photo, addressing evolving conference requirements.

The session concludes by examining prospects for the platform's continued development and growth.

items.title: Marketing automation and Drupal: tracking without evil
items.full_description:
greg.harvey

Mautic represents a free, open source marketing automation platform constructed on Symfony, mirroring Drupal's foundation.

By deploying Mautic through self-hosting rather than relying on commercial solutions like Eloqua or Marketo, organizations maintain authority over their data while preserving governance standards. Simultaneously, teams can engage in sophisticated user behavior monitoring and marketing automation activities. Since the software remains free and open source, developers can establish custom integrations and plugins tailored to organizational needs, rather than forcing organizational structures to conform to software limitations.

This presentation addresses the practical steps involved in deploying Mautic, establishing connections with Drupal websites, addressing GDPR and privacy compliance, and configuring Mautic functionality. The session demonstrates approaches to implementing transparent user tracking mechanisms while automating marketing operations—maintaining ethical standards regarding contact data management.

items.title: The future of digital experiences is ...?
items.full_description:
Ruth Cheesley
Mautic Project Lead

Ruth Cheesley explores how technological advancements will reshape the delivery and construction of digital experiences. The session addresses a key challenge facing technology providers: how to create seamless consumer experiences across multiple channels without relying on overly complex tool combinations that hinder scalability.

The presentation examines common obstacles that currently prevent unified digital experience delivery and discusses the negative consequences of poor digital experiences on both business outcomes and consumer satisfaction.

Cheesley highlights how open source platforms including Drupal and Mautic are positioned to meet future demands. The session concludes with forward-looking insights into potential deeper collaboration between these two platforms, offering attendees 'a glimpse of what lies ahead for a tighter integration between the two platforms.'

items.title: Understanding Automated Tests in Drupal
items.full_description:
Sujeet Kumar Verma, ridhimaabrol24

Deploying code to production can be nerve-wracking without proper safeguards. This session explores how Drupal 8's built-in testing framework can help developers maintain code quality and handle edge cases through multiple testing layers.

The presentation covers three main areas: how automated tests function within Drupal, the different testing layers available, and practical implementation through a live demonstration.

Topics Covered:
- Mechanics of automated testing in Drupal
- Various testing layers and their purposes
- Hands-on implementation strategies for custom modules

Prerequisites: Participants should have foundational knowledge of Drupal coding practices.

Key Learning Outcomes: Attendees will gain understanding of Drupal's automated testing capabilities, learn how different test layers differ from one another, and develop skills to write test cases for custom functionality and modules.

items.title: Utilizing QA Engineers throughout whole project lifecycle
items.full_description:
danielangelov

The presenter frames QA as more than a job title, describing it as 'a state of mind.' Using a reference to the 'Money Heist' series, they illustrate how technical QA engineers can identify bugs through documentation and architecture review, ultimately providing reproduction steps.

The session moves beyond routine task management and automation scripting to demonstrate how QA professionals can contribute value throughout multiple project phases:
- Pre-sale
- Discovery
- Creative
- Active development
- Handover

The core message emphasizes maximizing QA team potential by integrating their expertise across the entire project lifecycle rather than limiting their involvement to testing phases alone.

items.title: Write code once, run anywhere with Drupal & Flutter
items.full_description:
bibliophileaxe

With Drupal 9's release, the platform has moved toward becoming API-first. Decoupled architecture is gaining traction by offering flexibility and improved design capabilities. However, maintaining separate code bases for web and native applications remains a significant challenge. Flutter addresses this problem by enabling 'the same code can run anywhere – web, android, iOS.'

This session demonstrates building a basic Flutter application using Drupal 9 as a content delivery system. Key topics covered include evaluating Flutter's benefits, implementing secure app development, and optimizing code for cross-platform compatibility.

Learning Outcomes: Attendees will be able to construct a basic Flutter app with Drupal backend support, implement authentication between Flutter and Drupal APIs, and deploy the application across Android, iOS, and web platforms.

items.title: Drupal - choice of Australian government
items.full_description:
Alfred Deeb, Steven Worley
Salsa Digital

Over the past four years, Australian government jurisdictions at federal and state levels have adopted Drupal as their platform for public websites. The presentation explores how this open source solution addresses technical and non-technical challenges across government levels.

Alfred Deeb, founder of Salsa Digital, and Steven Worley, the company's whole-of-government platform architect, share insights from four major Australian government jurisdictions. They examine why Drupal succeeds in government contexts, how adoption has been encouraged, implementation trends across major jurisdictions, various architectural approaches, and how knowledge sharing between jurisdictions supports open government principles.

The session covers five key topics: factors behind Drupal's success in Australian government, government strategies promoting its adoption, regional adoption patterns, diverse implementation architectures, and collaborative knowledge exchange fostering transparency.

items.title: Feedback needed: dropping support for Internet Explorer 11 in Drupal 10 (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on dropping support for Internet Explorer 11 in Drupal 10.

Drupal core intends to discontinue Internet Explorer 11 compatibility with the release of Drupal 10. The session seeks input specifically from those utilizing assistive technology and accessibility professionals regarding current IE11 usage with screen readers, alternative browser support capabilities, and the practical feasibility of transitioning to different browsers.

items.title: Funding contribution so we can get more full-time makers (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on funding contribution for more full-time Drupal makers.

As Dries mentioned during the Driesnote, he'd love to see an almost tenfold increase of full-time contributors (~20 to ~200). While this idea is very ambitious and could have a huge impact on Drupal's growth, no-one seems to be talking about how we can actually fund this. Let's fix that.

items.title: Monitoring/observing Drupal on low-cost projects (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF panel session on monitoring and observing Drupal on low-cost projects.

Bigger Drupal sites always have complete monitoring stack, like BELK or TIG. However, these are overkill for smaller sites.

The panel addresses a practical challenge facing many organizations. While enterprise-level Drupal installations typically employ comprehensive monitoring solutions, smaller deployments often lack similar capabilities due to cost constraints.

The discussion acknowledges that pandemic-driven digital transformation increased reliance on online systems across all business sizes. Even modest websites now require assurances regarding uptime and performance reliability.

This session brought together practitioners to share affordable monitoring and observability approaches they've successfully implemented for budget-conscious Drupal projects.

items.title: Industrialised deployments of Drupal 8
items.full_description:
Thierry Delbart, Jean-François Bianco
Sopra Steria

The Occitanie region in southern France partnered with Sopra Steria to develop dependable cloud infrastructure and contemporary development approaches. These efforts aimed to fulfill government application standards for dependability and excellence.

The organization selected Drupal CMS to power certain services. Sopra Steria's architecture team integrated existing infrastructure with DevOps methods designed for Drupal 8 applications.

The presentation covers several key implementations: virtualizing Drupal through Bitnami containers for Docker and Kubernetes, approaches to configuration and content oversight, and the industrialization of continuous integration. These strategies enabled multiple developers to work concurrently while sustaining multiple testing environments.

The speakers brought complementary expertise: Jean François Bianco, an experienced Azure Cloud Infrastructure Architect, and Thierry Delbart, an Engineering Manager and senior Drupal developer at Sopra Steria, shared their hands-on experience.

items.title: Keynote: Building Diverse, Inclusive and Equitable Communities
items.full_description:
Siri Chilazi

The session focuses on creating communities and organizations that welcome diverse talents. Chilazi explains that 'unconscious (implicit) biases at the individual and systemic level can get in the way,' and traditional de-biasing approaches are costly and ineffective.

The keynote presents research-backed strategies for designing communities and processes that establish equitable conditions for all participants. Chilazi shares practical approaches grounded in behavioral research to incorporate diversity, inclusion, and equity into organizational structures and daily operations.

items.title: Realistic Valuation and Exit Strategies for your agency
items.full_description:
msilverman

This presentation examines realistic valuations for interactive agencies and the various exit options available at different business stages. The speaker emphasizes that timing is crucial—agencies should prepare advance planning to maximize available opportunities when considering a sale.

The session reviews three different agency sizes and the exit options each might realistically expect based on established industry practices.

items.title: Accessible Images, When It Matters Most
items.full_description:
cehfisher

During the COVID-19 pandemic, timely information distribution became crucial. With 65 percent of people being visual learners, creating accessible images became critical—especially for government public service announcements delivering urgent information to the public.

While adding alt text seems straightforward, accessible image creation involves many nuanced considerations. This session reviews different image categories, examines real-world examples from the pandemic, and identifies which design elements matter most for inclusive messaging.

Topics Covered: Different image types including decorative, informative, actionable, emotional, simple, and complex variants; accessibility considerations for images created during COVID-19; and essential design elements that make images more inclusive for diverse audiences.

items.title: An open company culture empowers autonomy and collaboration
items.full_description:
Tom Bamford
Annertech

The speaker emphasizes that an ideal work environment enables people to feel included, supported, and heard. He explores how organizations can cultivate such conditions while examining both the ethical dimensions and practical advantages of fostering openness.

Given the rise of remote and distributed work arrangements, traditional management approaches centered on direct oversight and fixed schedules are no longer viable. Instead, organizations benefit from establishing a shared vision grounded in core values. This foundation enables teams to operate with greater autonomy while maintaining collaborative relationships, empowering each individual to contribute meaningfully.

The presentation draws from the speaker's background working in the web industry, with nonprofit organizations, and his early experiences as a community facilitator in East Africa, where he first encountered open principles.

Key Learning Objectives:
- Grasp how transparency and individual ownership foster empowerment and advancement
- Apply insights from personal and professional experiences
- Advocate for inclusive decision-making and responsive listening across organizational levels

items.title: Community Working Group for healthier community (Panel)
items.full_description:
ultimike, jordana, gdemet, aburrows

The Drupal Community Working Group manages two key responsibilities: 'fostering a friendly community as well as maintaining and upholding the Code of Conduct.' During the past year, the group established a Community Health Team focused on implementing proactive initiatives to strengthen community wellness.

The panelists will outline their organizational framework and discuss completed efforts, current initiatives, and upcoming plans.

items.title: Creating Layouts and Landing Pages for Drupal 8
items.full_description:
pixelite

Landing pages present varied design challenges. Many site designs aren't built with content management systems in mind, requiring numerous distinct landing page layouts that often assume individual hand-crafting and styling.

The session addresses a core challenge: creating 'landing pages that are consistent so that users can understand them' while enabling non-technical editors to build them easily.

Topics Covered:
- Guidelines for designing structured and logical landing pages
- Creating a landing page component library
- Balancing visual variety with structural consistency
- Approaches to responsive landing pages

Learning Outcomes: Participants will understand how to select appropriate configuration approaches, learn benefits of tools like Layout Builder and Paragraphs, and discover key considerations for planning landing page content strategy.

items.title: Drupal in Higher Education (Panel)
items.full_description:
Paul Johnson (Chair), Adrian Ellison, Billy Wardrop, Iain Harper
CTI Digital / Universities

The higher education sector faces intense competition requiring strong digital presence. Yet new challenges complicate innovation efforts, including remote learning expansion, GDPR compliance, information security demands, and accessibility regulations.

The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the need for change, forcing universities to rapidly shift education online and reconsider recruitment strategies. These institutions must innovate at unprecedented speed.

Universities increasingly adopt Drupal to address these challenges and improve agility. The platform enables institutions to create user-centered digital experiences supporting student recruitment, enhance academic reputation, diversify revenue streams, and accelerate change implementation.

This panel brings together representatives from three universities with different scales, complexities, and legacy systems. They discuss how Drupal supports institutional success in this digital-dependent era, explore varying approaches between organizations, and examine encountered pitfalls and benefits.

items.title: Digital Asset Management (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on Digital Asset Management.

The session invites participants to engage in a Birds of a Feather discussion focused on Digital Asset Management solutions. Guiding questions include: 'Are you a user of an existing DAM? Are you evaluating DAM solutions? What's your use-case? Integration with Drupal?'

The primary objective is collaborative knowledge-sharing. 'During this BoF our goal is to share our experiences and gather yours about potential DAM solutions and use-cases.'

This format allows attendees with varying levels of DAM experience to discuss their current implementations, evaluation criteria, specific business needs, and how these tools might integrate with Drupal platforms.

items.title: Drupal Distributions: learning from each other (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session for Drupal Distribution developers.

A networking opportunity for Drupal Distribution developers to convene and exchange experiences.

Finn has contributed significantly to the LocalGov Drupal distribution throughout the year and has accumulated substantial knowledge from that work. Daniel Bosen, serving as lead developer at Thunder, indicated his intention to participate.

The session welcomes any additional professionals engaged in distribution development who wish to engage in discussion and collaborative learning.

items.title: Removing jQuery, jQueryUI and Backbone dependencies (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on removing jQuery, jQueryUI and Backbone dependencies from Drupal.

'Drupal is in the process of removing its dependencies on jQuery UI, jQuery and Backbone.'

The session focuses on the ongoing initiative within the Drupal project to eliminate reliance on these JavaScript libraries. Attendees can expect to learn about the strategic decisions being made as part of this modernization effort, understand the tasks remaining in the transition process, and discover opportunities for contributing to this work.

The Birds of a Feather format invites participants to ask questions about the initiative, raise any concerns or challenges they've identified, and engage in discussion with other community members involved in these efforts.

items.title: Virtual Coffee Calls to the rescue of usergroup experience (BoF)
items.full_description:
BoF session on Virtual Coffee Calls for the usergroup experience.

Due to the fact that coworking and real life meetups came to a halt in 2020, talking and exchange about topics and meeting with friends and colleagues became even harder.

The Virtual Lean Coffee Call format was presented as a solution to help people maintain connections during pandemic-related restrictions. This BoF session focused on how this approach enables professionals to stay engaged with colleagues and discuss topics of mutual interest when traditional in-person networking became impossible.

items.title: Front-end Web Performance Clinic 2020 (Workshop)
items.full_description:
mherchel, Ben Morss

Website performance critically impacts mission success, with conversion rates declining as page load times increase.

This workshop explores modern web performance in depth, covering topics including web performance metrics measurement and optimization, browser rendering mechanics, critical path analysis, JavaScript main thread optimization, and third-party script profiling.

Key learning areas encompass identifying which metrics matter most, optimizing for each metric, understanding how browsers render pages to enhance loading experiences, accounting for critical path impact, optimizing JavaScript execution, and profiling third-party scripts.

Prerequisites include foundational knowledge of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, basic familiarity with browser developer tools, and frustration with slow websites.

items.title: Visual regression testing
items.full_description:
joaogarin

This presentation covers visual regression testing fundamentals, including adaptation strategies for different use cases and integration into developer and team workflows. The speaker demonstrates tools in action and their benefits for design quality, accessibility, and usability.

The session targets 'everyone but most suited likely to frontend developers and designers.' No prior experience with visual testing is required to participate.

items.title: Tailor made Drupal Commerce
items.full_description:
Eirik Morland

Building atop open source software provides efficiency gains, yet introduces maintenance challenges. As custom modules proliferate alongside standard offerings, developers face pressure to abandon the broader ecosystem in favor of proprietary solutions.

Morland argues against this temptation. The presentation demonstrates technical and organizational approaches to managing growing custom codebases while maintaining active engagement with open source projects. Through disciplined practices, cultural values, and appropriate tooling, teams can confidently expand custom functionality without disconnecting from community contributions.

The core premise: 'Keeping the codebase up to date, while fixing problems in custom code can be tedious and frustration' drives consideration of forking. However, strategic solutions enable developers to navigate complexity while strengthening rather than undermining the open source ecosystem.

items.title: Design with empathy and agility to create equitable products (Panel)
items.full_description:
Joel Alcala, Terea Macomber
GRID Alternatives, Blue State

This panel discusses how innovation often involves analyzing and reframing problems rather than creating entirely new solutions. This approach proves especially important when serving underserved or low-income communities.

The speakers present a case study on the 'One Stop Shop,' a portal developed for California Air Resources Board (CARB). The platform assists low-income Californians in navigating clean energy and transportation incentive programs with complicated eligibility requirements.

'Often, innovation is less about creating new, shiny things and more about thorough analysis and reframing of the problem.' The team employed Design Thinking principles by conducting community research to build empathy, understanding user challenges, and developing solutions.

Development involved prototyping variations, testing with actual users, and iterating based on feedback. The technical implementation used Drupal and React with a flexible design system enabling responsiveness to user input.

The presenters share impact stories from the One Stop Shop beta launch in late 2019. They demonstrate how Design Thinking methodology can guide teams in creating products prioritizing accessibility, diversity, and inclusion.

items.title: The Drupal 10 initiative
items.full_description:
Drupal 9 will have a notably short major release lifecycle, with Drupal 10 planned for mid-2022 and Drupal 9 reaching end-of-life by late 2023.

This presentation explores the pathway from Drupal 9 to Drupal 10 and strategies for managing this transition. The speaker will reflect on lessons learned from the Drupal 8 to 9 upgrade process and outline improvements planned for version 10.

Audience participation is encouraged throughout the session.

items.title: There is a reason for that - read the source and learn
items.full_description:
"There is a module for that" represents a common approach when seeking solutions to recurring problems in Drupal development. Rather than reinventing functionality, developers search drupal.org for existing solutions.

Beyond finding ready-made modules, examining how Drupal core and popular contributed modules implement features proves valuable. Understanding code conventions, structural patterns, and design approaches helps improve your own work.

Issue queue discussions often reveal why code is written in particular ways. This session explores the reasoning behind Drupal coding decisions and practices that shape how the community builds solutions.

items.title: Why Automation knowledge is needed for Project managers
items.full_description:
Project managers should comprehend automation testing processes to align with industry standards and decrease reliance on specific personnel.

This session addresses those seeking to understand automation workflows and lead implementation independently. Key topics include why project managers need automation knowledge, its purpose and relevance to PM roles, managing automation backlogs without QA involvement, automation reporting systems, and problem statements.

The content targets QA and project managers interested in deepening their understanding of automation processes and workflows.

items.title: Writing Inclusive Documentation
items.full_description:
Documentation is only useful if people can read it, so it needs to be accessible. But what about making it inclusive? This session explores what that entails and how to ensure everyone benefits fully from your documentation while feeling like the intended audience.

Open source projects can sometimes make people feel unwelcome. The discussion covers strategies for clear writing despite technical terminology and complex ideas. It addresses what NOT to say in documentation—overlooked aspects that can exclude readers.

The session also reviews formatting, layout, and accessibility best practices, plus content strategy to ensure users have access to needed information.

Attendees will leave with an actionable list of items and fixes to apply to their documentation.

items.title: Decoupled Menu Initiative (BoF)
items.full_description:
At DrupalCon Global 2020, Dries proposed a new initiative for creating a decoupled menu component written in JavaScript. For Drupal to remain framework agnostic, he proposed to start with building components for Vue.js and React.js.

In this BoF, organizers want to invite everyone interested in helping out.

items.title: Drupal migrations (BoF)
Kuoni Congress (BoF)
items.full_description: Please come meet the Kuoni Congress team and speak about your experience with us, the OnAir platform, what you like and what you would have done differently.

items.title: Headless corporate website with integrated B2C shop
items.full_description:
This case study presents the implementation of a decoupled corporate website with integrated B2C-shop based on Drupal and Magento.

The website is operated by a large food producer and distributor in Switzerland. Advanced design and usability as well as an integrated look & feel across the different systems is crucial and therefore resulted in a headless system design which will be presented in this session.

This case study is targeted at business decision-makers evaluating a headless approach as well as technical experts interested in their implementation based on graphQL 4, nuxt, vue.js, and Kubernetes hosting.

items.title: Data Driven International Platforms
items.full_description:
Alexander Noakes
RNW Media (Netherlands)

How can an international team in the Netherlands build and scale a platform model for health, reproductive rights and inclusion that works for the country and the people where it is published and read? Using Drupal, Social APIs, Open Source tooling in a modern Data Lake, the presenter demonstrates how to deliver data driven content for users who need it but also measure its effectiveness and engagement over time and across platforms, in multiple languages and near real time insights.

This case study examines Love Matters, a pleasure-positive approach to Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) with regional teams in the Middle East, China, India, Mexico and Africa. The platform covers seven languages and multiple social media platforms per region.

Key topics include structuring multilingual taxonomies, aligning content, testing and tracking activity through social platforms, and using open source tools like Apache Airflow, BigQuery, and Metabase to create a data-driven feedback loop. The presentation covers both the Drupal CMS architecture and content strategy needed to publish engaging, factually correct articles while measuring engagement and demonstrating measurable outcomes for audiences seeking health information.

items.title: The Evolving Charts Ecosystem
items.full_description:
Users increasingly seek solutions for analyzing and visualizing data on the web. The Charts module enables site builders to create fully-featured charts, though users often desire additional features beyond standard offerings.

The concept of Drupal "ecosystems" emerged around 2011 to help users discover modules working together. Drupal.org maintainers formalized this by allowing navigation to "/ecosystem" on project pages.

An expanding ecosystem now supports the Charts module, which itself supports other ecosystems like Views and Webform. This session demonstrates leveraging the Charts ecosystem for data analysis and visualization needs, including:

- Building on-the-fly dashboards combining Charts with Core's Layout Builder
- Creating dynamic charts through Views Fields On/Off module integration
- Generating Charts with dynamic analysis via Views Simple Math field integration

items.title: Q&A with Drupal Association staff and board (Panel)
items.full_description: Want to know more about the Drupal Association's strategic goals and how it supports the Drupal Project? Join us for a question and answer session with the staff and board.

items.title: Setting up your digital project for success
items.full_description: The speaker discusses delivering a large-scale project involving 70 sites migrated to Drupal for a global brand within one year. Key topics include project structuring and planning approaches, using spreadsheets for tracking, establishing communication channels and governance frameworks, managing risks, planning quality assurance, and closing projects. The session offers guidance on multisite deployment lifecycles, designed for both project leaders and team members facing similar challenges with large digital initiatives.

items.title: State of Drupal Development Environments (Panel)
items.full_description:
Last year in Amsterdam, attendees confirmed that everyone had their own preferred Drupal development tool. This panel explores whether standardization is occurring or if diversity remains the norm.

At DrupalCon Global the discussion went to another level and some numbers were revealed, that showed Lando, Docker, Docksal and DDEV, followed closely by DrupalVM to be the clear igniters of Drupal local development.

The discussion examines the current landscape, introduces newer platforms like Cloud IDE and Launchpad, and explores each tool's roadmap and features. Panel creators discuss why they built their respective tools and the progress made since the previous year.

Attendees gain a comprehensive overview of available Drupal development environments for their specific project needs.

items.title: Top CMS Tools working together to build a more inclusive world
items.full_description:
The We4Authors Cluster brings together CMS developers from Drupal, Plone, SiteVision, and TinyMCE to explore accessibility best practices for content creation. Led by Funka, this European Commission-funded initiative focuses on making authoring tools more accessible and compliant with WCAG 2.1 AA guidelines.

Drupal is the most popular CMS used by governments in the EU and plays a significant role in meeting the Web Accessibility Directive requirements. OpenConcept serves as Senior Advisor, building on prior work implementing Authoring Tool Accessibility Guidelines (ATAG) 2.0 in Drupal.

Participants will learn about authoring tool impacts on site accessibility, best practices across publishing platforms, Drupal's ATAG 2.0 adoption leadership, user testing results from prototypes, and implications for EU Web Accessibility Directive compliance. The initiative's findings will be shared broadly to advance accessibility standards across platforms.

items.title: Understanding Marketing
items.full_description:
Marketers are an increasingly important audience for Drupal. Come to this session to learn what our Marketing colleagues do, what they care about and how they measure success.

Attendees will gain better communication skills for conveying their work and value to marketing professionals. This presentation builds upon a previous iteration delivered at DrupalCon Global.

items.title: Components module feature requests and discussions (BoF)
items.full_description: Discuss features you'd like to see in the Components module. Or dreams of how you'd like the Drupal theme system to work.

items.title: Triage novice issues with Mentors
Drupal loves NoSQL databases
items.full_description:
Drupal is a powerful CMS that typically relies on SQL databases, but these don't suit every use case. NoSQL databases offer advantages for large or constantly evolving datasets, yet Drupal core lacks native support, often causing database performance issues.

The External entities module bridges this gap by leveraging Drupal's database-agnostic Entity API to work with external databases. While content lives external, Drupal sees those remote entities as internal. This enables field customization, references, comments, aliases, and commerce integration.

The presenters share their experience serving approximately 1 million entities from Elasticsearch. The session covers their rationale for this approach, explores benefits and limitations, and discusses additional possibilities the module unlocks.

items.title: The Olivero theme: Genesis and Update
items.full_description:
Starting out as a discussion in a lobby at DrupalCon Seattle, the Olivero theme is now an official Drupal core strategic initiative, and aims to become the new default front-end theme for Drupal 9.1!

In this session, the speaker walks attendees through the genesis of the theme concept, provides an overview of challenges encountered, and demonstrates the current status along with upcoming features in the pipeline.

items.title: Trivia Night
items.full_description:
Test out your Drupal knowledge! In the grand tradition of pub quizzes, there will be 6/7 rounds of 10 questions covering all things Drupal, and a few more questions about general web topics.

Participants will form teams of five to compete for the title of Drupal trivia champions and win prizes.
